parts.ask: Particle of mass 2 kg with velocity (5i + 3j) m/s receives impulse I = ai + bj N s, after which its velocity is λ(i + j) m/s; |I| = √40: find the two possible impulses
parts.ms: M1 I = m(v − u); A1 2(λ − 5)i + 2(λ − 3)j; M1 Pythagoras with √40: (λ − 5)² + (λ − 3)² = 10; DM1 solve λ² − 8λ + 12 = 0 (λ = 2, 6); A1 both impulses. Alt: a + 10 = b + 6 with a² + b² = 40 (MS p.7)

parts.ms: B1 driving force 3P/12 (or P/12); M1A1 uphill: 3P/12 − R − 9000/15 = 0; M1A1A1 downhill: P/12 + 9000/15 − R = (9000/9.8)(9.8/20) = 450 (A1 at most one error, A1 correct); DM1 solve; A1 one correct; A1 both. parts.ms: B1 F = μR at least once; M1A1 resolve horizontally S = (4/5)R; M1A1 resolve vertically (3/5)S + R = 25g; M1A1 moments, e.g. M(A): 25g × 1.5 cos θ = S × 3 sin θ + (3/5)S × 3 cos θ; DM1 form an equation in tan θ only; A1 13/40. parts.ask: Particle of mass 6 kg projected at 14 m/s up a rough ramp AB (15 m, tan α = 5/12, μ = 0.25): find the work done against friction from A to B
parts.ms: B1 R = 6g cos α; M1 work = 15 × 0.25 × R; A1 204 or 200 (MS p.12)

parts.command: Use the work-energy principle to find
parts.ask: P leaves the ramp at B with speed v and lands on the ground at C with speed w: use the work-energy principle to find (i) v, (ii) w
parts.ms: Work-energy required (suvat solutions not accepted). M1 initial KE − GPE − work = final KE; A1ft at most one error; A1ft ½(6)(14²) − 6g(15)(5/13) − 6g(15)(3/13) = ½(6)v² (the last term is the work against friction); A1 3.88; M1 energy equation for w; A1ft ½(6)(14²) − 6g(15)(3/13) = ½(6)w² (A to C: no net height change) or ½mw² = ½mv² + mg(75/13); A1 11.3 (MS p.12)

parts.ms: M1A1 KE equation for B: 48mu²/25 = ½mw² − ½mu² ⇒ w = 11u/5; M1A1 CLM 3m(2u) + mu = 3mv + mw ⇒ v = 8u/5; M1A1 impact law w − v = e(2u − u); DM1 solve; A1 3/5 (MS p.13)

parts.ask: B hits a smooth wall (coefficient f) and rebounds with speed equal to A's speed after the first collision: find f
parts.ms: M1 fw = v, condone sign error; A1 8/11 (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Ball projected from O on horizontal ground with velocity (pi + qj) m/s; at t = 3 s it passes A with velocity (8i − 12j) m/s: find the speed of projection
parts.ms: B1 p = 8; M1 −12 = q − 3g; A1 q = 17.4; M1 Pythagoras (independent); A1 19.2 or 19 (MS p.14)

parts.ask: For an interval of T seconds the speed v satisfies v ≤ 10: find T
parts.ms: M1 Pythagoras for the vertical component; A1 ±6; DM1 suvat for the time, e.g. −6 = 6 − 9.8T; A1 1.22 or 1.2. Alt: 8² + (17.4 − gt)² = 100 (MS p.14)

parts.ask: At B on the path the direction of motion is perpendicular to that at A: find the vertical height of B above A
parts.ms: M1 vertical component at B from the perpendicular direction: (2/3) × 8 = 16/3; A1; DM1 v² = u² + 2as between B and A: (−12)² = (16/3)² − 2g(−h); A1 5.90. Alt: time from the scalar product then s = vt − ½gt² (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Car of mass 600 kg, constant power P W, resistance R N: on a level road at 15 m/s the acceleration has magnitude 0.2 m/s²; up a road inclined at θ (sin θ = 1/20) it has constant speed 10 m/s: find P
parts.ms: M1 P = 15F₁ or 10F₂; M1 F₁ − R = 600 × 0.2; A1 P/15 − R = 120; M1 uphill equation with F₂ ≠ F₁; A1 at most one error; A1 P/10 − R − 30g = 0; DM1 solve; A1 5220 or 5200 (MS p.11)

parts.ask: Rigid framework shaped like the digit "4" from uniform rods AB (6a), BC (5a), CD (4a), with E on AB and CD, BE = 4a, CE = 3a, angle CEB = 90°; suspended from B, BA makes θ with the downward vertical: find θ to the nearest degree
parts.ms: M1A1A1 moments about an axis perpendicular to AB: 6m(3a) + 4m(4a) + 5m(2a) = 15m ȳ ⇒ ȳ = 44a/15 from B; M1A1A1 moments about AB: 5m(3a/2) + 4m(a) = 15m x̄ ⇒ x̄ = 23a/30; M1 tan θ = x̄/ȳ from B; A1ft 23/88; A1 15 (14.64…) to the nearest degree. Special cases if a is omitted (MS p.12)

parts.ask: v = (5t² − 12t + 15)i + (t² + 8t − 10)j, P starts at O: at time T it moves in the direction of i + j: find T
parts.ms: M1 equate components, 5T² − 12T + 15 = T² + 8T − 10; A1 4T² − 20T + 25 = 0; A1 5/2 (MS p.13)

parts.ask: P is at A when t = 3: find the magnitude of the acceleration at A
parts.ms: M1 differentiate; A1 a = 18i + 14j at t = 3; DM1 Pythagoras; A1 √520, 22.8 (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Find the position vector of A
parts.ms: M1 integrate (powers up); A1 at most one error; A1 r = (5t³/3 − 6t² + 15t)i + (t³/3 + 4t² − 10t)j; A1 36i + 15j (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Uniform ladder AB (6 m, 30 kg) at 60° to the horizontal, A on rough ground, B against a smooth wall; a man (70 kg) stands at C, AC = 2 m: find the magnitude of the force exerted on the ladder by the ground
parts.ms: M1 M(A): 3(30g) cos 60° + 2(70g) cos 60° = 6N sin 60°, all terms; A1 correct; B1 R = 100g; B1 F = N = 115g/(3√3) ≈ 217; DM1 Pythagoras; A1 1000 (MS p.14)

parts.ask: The man climbs to D where the ladder is about to slip; μ = 0.4: find AD
parts.ms: M1 F = 0.4 × 100g (= 392); M1 moments about A with x for the man; A1 40g × 3√3 = 35gx + 45g; A1 4.65 (MS p.14)

parts.ask: State how the modelling assumption that the ladder is a rod has been used
parts.final_form: one valid statement, no incorrect statements
parts.ms: B1 e.g. the ladder does not bend; it meets the wall/floor at a point; its weight acts at a single point (MS pp.14–15)

parts.ask: Particle projected from A, 20 m above O on horizontal ground, at 12 m/s at θ° above the horizontal; it hits the ground at B (OB = 40 m) at t = 5 s: by considering energy, find its speed at B
parts.ms: M1 conservation of energy, all terms; A1 at most one error; A1 ½m(144) + mg(20) = ½mv²; A1 23 or 23.2 (MS p.15)

parts.ask: Find the least speed of P as it moves from A to B
parts.ms: M1 horizontal motion 12 cos θ × 5 = 40; A1 minimum speed 12 cos θ = 8, final answer (MS p.15)

parts.ask: Find the length of time for which the speed of P is more than 10 m/s
parts.ms: B1ft vertical component 6 when the speed is 10; M1 vertical speed 6 = 12 sin θ − gt; A1 with sin θ = √5/3 (cos θ = 2/3 from (b)), one time or the interval (t = 0.30, 1.52); A1 interval 1.22 s; M1 required time 5 − 1.22; A1 3.78 or 3.8. Alts: −6 = 6 − gt (12/g), or energy for the height (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: A (3m) and B (4m) moving towards each other collide directly; afterwards both move the same way with speeds u/3 (A) and u (B); A receives an impulse of magnitude 8mu: find the coefficient of restitution
parts.ms: M1A1 impulse on A: 8mu = 3mv − 3m(u/3) ⇒ A's initial speed 3u; M1A1 impulse on B (or CLM) ⇒ B's initial speed u; M1 impact law u − u/3 = e(3u + u); A1 1/6. A double sign error in CLM combined with w = −u scores max 4/6 (MS p.17)

parts.ask: The collision is at distance d from a smooth wall; B hits the wall (e = 1/4) and rebounds, meeting A again at distance x from the wall: find x in terms of d
parts.ms: B1 gap 2d/3 when B reaches the wall; B1 rebound speed u/4; M1 time to close the gap (2d/3)/(u/3 + u/4); A1 8d/(7u); DM1 distance from the wall (8d/(7u))(u/4); A1 2d/7. Alt: equate times for A and B to reach the meeting point, 3d − 3x = d + 4x (MS pp.17–18)

parts.final_form: V = 26.3 or 26 (the exact (49 + 22√14)/5 is not accepted: g = 9.8 used)
parts.ms: B1 driving force 3500/V; M1 equation of motion, all terms, condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion; A1 3500/V − 20V + 40g = 0; M1 form a 3-term quadratic 20V² − 392V − 3500 = 0; A1 26.3 or 26, not (49 + 22√14)/5 (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Particle of mass 1.5 kg with v = (5t² − t³)i + (2t³ − 8t)j: find the force F when t = 2
parts.ms: M1 differentiate (powers down); A1 a = (10t − 3t²)i + (6t² − 8)j; DM1 substitute t = 2 and F = ma; A1 12i + 24j, ignore any magnitude (MS p.9)

parts.ask: P starts at the origin: find its position vector when it is moving in the direction of j
parts.final_form: r = (625/12)i + (425/2)j, exact or decimals 52i + 210j or better (52.083…i + 212.5j)
parts.ms: B1 5t² − t³ = 0 ⇒ t = 5; M1 integrate (powers up); A1 r = (5t³/3 − t⁴/4)i + (t⁴/2 − 4t²)j (no constant since r = 0 at t = 0); A1 625/12 i + 425/2 j, or 52i + 210j or better (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Template T = square ABCD (side 6a) minus right-angled triangle EFG (EF = EG = 4a, a from AB and AD) minus circle (radius a, centre H on AC, 2a from BC): show its centre of mass is 4(67 − 3π)a/(3(28 − π)) from AD
parts.ms: B1 mass ratio 36 : 8 : π : 28 − π; B1 distances from AD 3a, 7a/3, 4a (or a parallel axis); M1 moments, all terms; A1 36(3a) − 8(7a/3) − π(4a) = (28 − π)d; A1* given answer; finding the distance from BC instead, (236 − 6π)a/(3(28 − π)), is allowed 4/5 (MS p.10)

parts.ask: T hangs with AB horizontal from two vertical strings at A and B; weight W, tension at B is kW: find k to 2 d.p.
parts.ms: M1 M(A): W × 4(67 − 3π)a/(3(28 − π)) = kW × 6a (or resolve and take moments about the centre of mass); A1 correct equation (distance ≈ 3.088a); A1 0.51 (MS p.10)

parts.ask: Particle of mass 0.3 kg moving at 5 m/s receives a horizontal impulse J N s at 60° to its direction of motion; its speed afterwards is 8 m/s: find J
parts.ms: M1A1 impulse-momentum parallel (or perpendicular) to the original direction; M1A1 second component equation (a correct vector equation earns all 4); DM1 eliminate to J² + 1.5J − 3.51 = 0; A1 1.3 or better. Alt: momentum triangle with the cosine rule 2.4² = J² + 1.5² − 3J cos 120°. Taking the final velocity parallel to the initial velocity or to the impulse is a method error, not a misread (MS pp.11–12)

parts.ask: Uniform rod (8a, mass M) hinged to a wall at A, held by a string from B (AB = 5a) to C on the wall 5a above A, angle BAC = 70°: find the tension in terms of M and g
parts.final_form: T = 4 cos 20° Mg/(5 sin 55°) ≈ 0.918Mg (exact or 0.92Mg or better)
parts.ms: M1 moments about A, condone sign errors, angle errors and sin/cos confusion; A1 5a × T sin 55° = 4a cos 20° × Mg; A1 exact or 0.92Mg (MS p.13)

parts.ask: The force on the rod at A has magnitude λMg: find λ to 2 s.f.
parts.ms: M1A1 resolve vertically Mg = V + T cos 55° (V ≈ 0.474Mg); M1A1 resolve horizontally H = T sin 55° (H ≈ 0.752Mg); M1 Pythagoras; A1 0.89. Alt: moments about B and about C (MS pp.13–14)

parts.ask: A (2 kg) on a rough ramp (tan θ = 5/12, μ = 3/8) connected over a smooth pulley at the top to B (3 kg) hanging 2 m above the ground; released from rest: find the potential energy lost by the system as A moves 2 m up the ramp
parts.ms: M1 GPE lost, all terms; A1 3g × 2 − 2g × 2 sin θ; A1 58g/13, 43.7 or 44, must be positive (MS p.15)

parts.ask: Find the work done against friction as A moves 2 m up the ramp

parts.command: Use the work-energy principle to find
parts.ask: Use the work-energy principle to find the speed of B just before it hits the ground
parts.final_form: 3.47 or 3.5 m s⁻¹ (3 or 2 s.f.); g must be substituted, so the exact √(16g/13) is not a final answer
parts.ms: M1 KE gained = GPE lost − work against friction, no extra terms; A2ft ½(2 + 3)v² = (a) − (b) (−1 each error); A1 3.47 or 3.5, g substituted (MS p.15)

parts.command: Use the work-energy principle to find
parts.ask: B does not rebound; A continues and comes to instantaneous rest at Y with XY = (2 + d) m: use the work-energy principle to find d
parts.ms: M1 KE lost = GPE gained + work against friction for A alone; A2ft ½(2)(16g/13) = 2g d sin θ + d(9g/13) (−1 each error); A1 16/19 (g cancels) (MS p.15)

parts.ask: Ball projected from A on horizontal ground with velocity (6i + 12j) m/s lands at B: find AB
parts.ms: M1 suvat for the time (−12 = 12 − gt); A1 t = 24/g (2.45); M1 AB = 6t; A1 14.7 or 15, g not left in the denominator (MS p.17)

parts.ask: When the ball is more than h m above the ground its speed is less than 10 m/s: find the smallest possible h
parts.ms: B1 vertical component ±8 when the speed is 10; M1 v² = u² + 2as for h; A1 8² = 12² − 2gh; A1 4.08 or 4.1. Alts: times from 12 − gt = ±8, or energy ½m(10²) + mgh = ½m(12² + 6²) (MS p.17)

parts.ask: At C the direction of motion is perpendicular to the direction just before hitting the ground at B: find the velocity at C in terms of i and j
parts.final_form: v = 6i + 3j (a vector in i and j)
parts.ms: M1 scalar product (6, −12)·(6, v) = 0 or equivalent for the vertical component at C; A1 3; A1 6i + 3j; 6i − 3j from (6, 12) is treated as a misread, M1A0A0 (MS p.18)

parts.ask: A (2m), B (m), C (3m) at rest in a line on a smooth plane; A projected at 2u hits B; e for each pair: (i) show B's speed after is (4/3)u(1 + e), (ii) find A's speed after
parts.ms: M1A1 CLM 4mu = 2mv + mw; M1A1 impact law w − v = 2ue, signs consistent; DM1 solve; A1* given w; A1 v = (2/3)u(2 − e), must be positive (MS p.19)

parts.ask: At the instant A hits B, C is projected at speed u towards B and B, C collide directly: show there will be a second collision between A and B
parts.final_form: reasoned conclusion: B moves back towards A while A still moves towards B, so they collide
parts.ms: B1 A still moves towards B since 2 > e; M1 CLM and impact law for B–C; A1 both equations, e.g. (4/3)eu − (5/3)u = x + 3y and y − x = e(u + (4u + 4eu)/3); DM1 solve for x (B's velocity); A1 x = −(5/12)u − (17/12)ue − ue² (or a multiple); A1* since e, u > 0, B moves back towards A, hence a collision. Alt: consider C's direction (MS pp.19–20)

parts.ask: Particle of mass m pushed a distance d up a line of greatest slope of a rough plane (tan α = 5/12, μ = 1/5): show the work done against friction is 12mgd/65
parts.ms: B1 F = μR = (1/5)mg cos α; M1 work = force × distance; A1* (1/5)mg(12/13)d = 12mgd/65 (MS p.7)

parts.command: Use the work-energy principle to find
parts.ask: The particle is released from rest at B: use the work-energy principle to find its speed on reaching A, in terms of g and d
parts.ms: M1 work-energy equation, all terms, condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion; A1 at most one error; A1 ½mv² = mgd(5/13) − 12mgd/65 (= 13mgd/65); A1 √(2gd/5) or exact equivalent (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Uniform pole AB (2.5 m, 70 N), end B against a rough vertical wall, held by a cable AC (4 m) to C on the wall 2.5 m above B, cable at α to the wall (tan α = 3/4): show the tension is 56 N
parts.ms: M1 moments about B, condone sin/cos confusion and angle errors; A1 at most one error; A1 T × 2.5 sin α = 70 × 1.25 sin 2α (or similar triangles); A1* T = 70 × 4/5 = 56 from exact working (MS p.10)

parts.ask: A (2m) and B (3m) moving towards each other collide directly; afterwards they move apart with the same speed v; A receives an impulse of magnitude 5mv: find the coefficient of restitution
parts.ms: M1A1 impulse on A: 5mv = 2m(v − (−x)) ⇒ x = 3v/2; M1A1 impulse on B or CLM ⇒ y = 2v/3; M1 impact law 2v = e(3v/2 + 2v/3); A1 12/13 (MS p.11)

parts.ask: B then strikes a smooth fixed wall (coefficient f) and rebounds; B's total KE loss from both impacts is E, and A's KE loss in the collision is 2E: find f
parts.ms: B1 B's speed after the wall vf; M1 KE equation in f, e.g. 2 × ½(3m)(y² − (vf)²) = ½(2m)(x² − v²) (2 on the wrong side condoned); A1 correct equation; A1 1/6 cao — √31/6 comes from inconsistent subtraction (MS p.11)

parts.ask: Lamina = rectangle ABCE (AB = EC = a, AE = BC = d) plus sector CDE (centre C, radius a, angle π/3); its centre of mass lies on EC: show a = √3 d
parts.ms: B1 sector centre of mass 2a sin(π/6)/(3 × π/6) = 2a/π from C, from the formulae book; M1 moments about EC (parallel axis allowed); A1 ad(d/2) = (πa²/6)(2a/π) sin(π/6); A1* a = √3 d (MS p.12)

parts.ask: The lamina is freely suspended from B and hangs with BC at β radians to the downward vertical: find β
parts.ms: B1 mass ratio a²/√3 : πa²/6 : sum; M1 moments about BC; A1ft correct equation; A1 distance from BC = 6a/(6 + √3π) (or 6d/(2√3 + π)); M1 trig for a relevant angle; A1ft tan β = (their distance)/d; A1 0.737 or 0.74 (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Particle projected from A, h m above ground, at 10 m/s; it hits the ground at B after 2.5 s with speed 18 m/s: by considering energy, find h
parts.ms: M1 conservation of energy, all three terms; A1 ½m(10²) + mgh = ½m(18²); A1 11.4 or 11 (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Find the distance OB
parts.ms: M1 vertical suvat to find the projection angle; A1ft 10 sin α (2.5) − ½g(2.5²) = −11.4; A1 α = 50.2° (or v_V = 7.77); M1 horizontal distance 10 cos α × 2.5; A1 16.0 or 16 (MS p.13)

parts.ask: The speed of P is at most 8 m/s for T seconds: find T
parts.ms: M1 energy for the height where the speed is 8 (1.84 m above A); A1 1.8 or better; M1 suvat equation in t; A1 1.84 = 10 sin 50.2° t − 4.9t²; DM1 difference of the roots; A1 0.98 or 0.978. Alts: vertical speed ±4.8 via Pythagoras, or a quadratic from |v| = 8 (MS pp.13–14)

parts.ask: Particle of mass 0.5 kg with velocity (2i + 4j) m/s receives an impulse (−4i + 6j) N s: find its speed immediately afterwards
parts.ms: M1 I = mv − mu (subtraction in the wrong order condoned); A1 correct equation; A1 v = −6i + 16j; M1 Pythagoras on their v; A1 √292 = 2√73 or 17 or better; 5/5 allowed working from the negative of v (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Find the angle between the directions of motion immediately before and immediately after the impulse
parts.ms: M1 trig for the two relevant angles (e.g. 69.44°, 63.43°) for their v; A1ft θ = 180° − tan⁻¹(16/6) − tan⁻¹(4/2); A1 47° or better; alt: scalar product cos θ = (−12 + 64)/(√20 √292) (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Car (600 kg) tows trailer (200 kg) by a light towbar up a road inclined at θ (sin θ = 1/20); resistances 150 N (car) and 300 N (trailer); engine at P kW gives constant speed 15 m/s: find P
parts.final_form: P = 12.6 or 13 (kW); 12600 as the final answer scores 4/5
parts.ms: M1 equation for the whole system, all terms; A1 at most one error; A1 F − 300 − 150 − 200g/20 − 600g/20 = 0 (F = 842); M1 P = Fv; A1 12.6 or 13 (MS p.8)

parts.command: Use the work-energy principle to find
parts.ask: At 20 m/s the towbar breaks at X; the trailer (resistance 300 N) comes to instantaneous rest at Y: use the work-energy principle to find XY
parts.ms: M1 work-energy for the trailer only: KE lost = GPE gained + work against resistance; A1 at most one error; A1 ½(200)(400) = (200g/20)d + 300d; A1 101 or 100 (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Particle of mass 0.25 kg with v = (6 sin 3t)i + (1 + 2 cos t)j: find the force F in terms of t
parts.final_form: F = (9/2) cos 3t i − ½ sin t j
parts.ms: M1 differentiate v; M1 F = ma in vectors; A1 (9/2)cos 3t i − ½ sin t j or equivalent (MS p.9)

parts.ask: At t = 0 the position vector is (4i − √3 j) m: find the position vector when P is first moving parallel to i
parts.ms: M1 set the j-component of v to zero; A1 t = 2π/3 (120° alone loses this and the final mark); M1 integrate v (constant optional); M1 use r(0) = 4i − √3 j for the constant, e.g. r = (6 − 2cos 3t)i + (t + 2 sin t − √3)j; A1 one component correct; A1 4i + (2π/3)j, ISW (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Balls A (2m, speed 2u) and B (3m, speed u) moving in opposite directions collide directly, coefficient e: show B's speed afterwards is u(1 + 6e)/5
parts.ms: M1 CLM, condone sign errors; A1 4mu − 3mu = 3mw − 2mv; M1 impact law; A1 v + w = 3eu, signs consistent; DM1 solve; A1* given answer (MS p.10)

parts.ask: B then hits a smooth fixed wall (e = 5/7) and rebounds; there is a second A–B collision: find the range of possible values of e
parts.ms: B1 A's velocity after (9e − 1)u/5 in B's direction (or equivalent for their directions); B1 B's rebound speed (5/7)(1 + 6e)u/5; M1 inequality (5/7)(1 + 6e)u/5 > (9e − 1)u/5; A1 e < 4/11, lower limit optional but if given must be strict (MS p.10)

parts.ask: Smooth hemisphere (centre O, radius 5a) fixed on rough ground; uniform rod AB (16a, weight W) rests on it at C (AC = 12a) with A on the ground: explain why AO = 13a
parts.ms: B1* the rod is a tangent so angle ACO is a right angle, giving a 5a, 12a, 13a triangle (MS p.11)

parts.ask: The normal reaction at C is kW: show k = 8/13
parts.ms: M1 moments about A, condone sin/cos confusion; A1 W × 8a × 12/13 = kW × 12a; A1* given answer with cos α substituted and a final statement (MS p.11)

parts.ask: The resultant force at A has magnitude R acting upwards at θ° to the horizontal: find (i) R in terms of W, (ii) θ
parts.ms: M1A1 resolve horizontally R_H = kW sin α = 40W/169; M1A1 resolve vertically R_V = W − kW cos α = 73W/169; DM1 Pythagoras; A1 √6929 W/169 = √41 W/13, accept 0.49W; DM1 tan θ = 73/40; A1 61 or better. Alts: resolve along/perpendicular to the rod (P = 5W/13, Q = 4W/13), or a triangle of forces with the cosine rule (MS pp.11–12)

parts.ask: Uniform wire framework: straight ABC (25a), straight ADE (24a), semicircular arc ABD (radius 7a), EC = 7a, angle AEC = 90°: show the centre of mass is 53a/(2(7 + π)) from AE
parts.ms: B1 mass ratio 24a : 25a : 7πa : 7a (7 + π); M1 moments about AE with all terms; A1 25a(7a/2) + 7πa(14a/π) = 7a(7 + π)d; A1* given answer (MS p.13)

parts.ask: The framework is freely suspended from A and hangs with AC at α° to the downward vertical: find α
parts.ms: B1 arc centre of mass 7a below A (17a above E); M1 moments about a horizontal axis through A; A1 24a(12a) + 25a(12a) + 7πa(7a) = 7a(7 + π)ȳ; A1 ȳ = 7a(12 + π)/(7 + π); DM1 angle tan⁻¹(d/ȳ) = tan⁻¹(53/(14(12 + π))) ≈ 14.04°; DM1 α = tan⁻¹(7/24) − that angle; A1 2.2 or better (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Particle projected from O with speed u at α above the horizontal: show y = x tan α − (gx²/(2u²))(1 + tan²α)
parts.ms: M1A1 x = ut cos α; M1A1 y = ut sin α − ½gt²; DM1 eliminate t; A1* given answer, sec²α allowed, final step explained (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Ball projected from O at 20 m/s at θ°; a 2 m vertical pole stands 10 m away: find the range of θ for which the ball passes over the pole
parts.ms: M1 substitute u = 20, x = 10, y = 2 to form a quadratic in tan θ (=, < or > allowed); A1 one critical value 18.6° or 82.7°; A1 18.6 < θ < 82.7 (MS p.14)

parts.ask: With θ = 40, find the speed of the ball as it passes over the pole
parts.ms: M1 use the given formula for the height at x = 10; A1 y = 6.30 m; DM1 energy, all 3 terms; A1ft ½mv² = ½m(400) − mgy; A1 17 or 16.6. Alt: components via time 0.653 s, v_V ≈ 6.46, v_H = 20 cos 40° (MS pp.14–15)

parts.ask: The ball first hits the ground at C: find OC
parts.ms: M1 complete method, e.g. y = 0 in the trajectory, time of flight, or range 20² sin 80°/g; A1 40 or 40.2 (MS p.15)

parts.ask: r = (t³ − 8t)i + (t³/3 − t² + 2t)j: find the acceleration of P when t = 4
parts.ms: M1 differentiate r (powers down, at least 2); A1 v = (3t² − 8)i + (t² − 2t + 2)j; M1 differentiate again; A1 a = 6ti + (2t − 2)j; A1 24i + 6j stated as a simplified vector, ISW (MS p.7)

parts.ask: At time T, P moves in the direction of 2i + j: find T
parts.ms: M1 equation using the direction (i-component = 2 × j-component), condone the 2 on the wrong side; A1ft 3T² − 8 = 2(T² − 2T + 2), i.e. T² + 4T − 12 = 0; A1 T = 2 only (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Particle on a smooth floor between parallel smooth walls 3d apart, starting at A (d from YZ) with speed u towards YZ; e = 2/3 at each wall: find the time T₁ to bounce off each wall once and return to A
parts.ms: B1 speed after first impact (2/3)u; B1 speed after second impact (4/9)u; M1 total time with all 3 stages, dimensionally correct; A1 d/u + 3d/(2u/3) + 2d/(4u/9) = d/u + 9d/(2u) + 18d/(4u); A1 10d/u (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Find the further time T₂ to bounce off each wall once more and return to A again
parts.ms: B1ft T₂ = (9/4)T₁ (speeds now 4/9 of before), i.e. 45d/(2u) or equivalent (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Particle of mass 0.5 kg with velocity λ(i + j) m/s receives an impulse of magnitude √(5/2) N s, after which its velocity is 4i m/s: find the two possible values of λ
parts.ms: M1 I = mv − mu (must subtract); A1 I = 0.5((4 − λ)i − λj); M1 magnitude (Pythagoras) to form an equation in λ; A1ft 5/2 = ¼((4 − λ)² + λ²); DM1 three-term quadratic (2λ² − 8λ + 6 = 0); A1cso λ = 3 and λ = 1. Alt: vector triangle with cosine rule using the 45° angle (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Uniform rod AB (4 m, 50 N), end A on rough ground, held at α to the ground (sin α = 3/5) by a cable at B perpendicular to the rod: show T = 20
parts.ms: M1 moments about A, condone sin/cos confusion (50g is an accuracy error); A1 4T = 2 cos α × 50 with cos α = 4/5 seen; A1* given answer, 4/5 used correctly (MS p.11)

parts.ask: The rod is in limiting equilibrium: find the coefficient of friction between rod and ground
parts.ms: M1A1 resolve horizontally H = T sin α; M1A1 resolve vertically T cos α + V = 50 (either can be replaced by a moments equation or by resolving along/perpendicular to the rod); M1 F = μR used with values; A1 6/17, 0.35 or better, accept 12/34 (MS p.11)

parts.ask: P (mass km, speed x) and Q (mass m, speed y) moving towards each other collide; afterwards both move the same way with speeds v (P) and 2v (Q); e = 1/5; impulse on Q has magnitude 5mv: find (i) y, (ii) x in terms of v, (iii) k
parts.ms: Three equations needed, one the impact law, marked in the order seen: M1A1 impulse-momentum for Q: 5mv = m(2v − (−y)) (or for P); M1A1 CLM kmx − my = kmv + 2mv (or second impulse equation); M1A1 NEL 2v − v = (1/5)(x + y), e on the correct side; A1 y = 3v; A1 x = 2v; A1 k = 5 (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Find, in terms of m and v, the total kinetic energy lost in the collision
parts.ms: M1 KE lost (or change in KE), complete substituted expression; A1ft ½km(x² − v²) + ½m(y² − 4v²); A1 10mv² only (KE before 14.5mv², after 4.5mv²) (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Template from three laminas: square PQUV (side 3a, density k), square URST (side 6a, density k), right-angled triangle QRU (UQ = 3a, UR = 6a, density 2k): show its centre of mass is 29a/14 from QT
parts.ms: B1 mass ratios 1 : 4 : 2 : 7 (9, 36, 18, 63); B1 distances from QT −3a/2, 3a, 2a (signs consistent); M1 moments about QT; A1 18(2a) + 36(3a) − 9(3a/2) = 63d; A1* given answer with an interim step collecting the a terms, a in the final answer (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Template freely suspended from Q hangs with QR at θ° to the downward vertical: find θ
parts.ms: B1 vertical distances from Q (or another parallel axis) 3a/2, 6a, 2a; M1 moments about PQ; A1 9(3a/2) + 18(2a) + 36(6a) = 63v̄; A1 v̄ = 59a/14 (4.2a or better); M1 trig with their v̄ for a relevant angle, tan⁻¹(29/59) ≈ 26.18°; M1 required angle = tan⁻¹2 − tan⁻¹(29/59); A1 37.3, 37 or better (MS pp.13–14)

parts.ask: Particle of mass 3 kg projected up a rough ramp AB (4 m, tan α = 1/6, μ = 3/4): find the work done against friction from A to B
parts.final_form: 87.0 or 87 J (2 or 3 s.f.; not as a multiple of g)
parts.ms: B1 R = 3g cos α = 18g/√37 (= 29.0); M1 F = ¾R; M1 work = 4F; A1 87.0 or 87, a multiple of g not allowed (MS p.14)

parts.command: Use the work-energy principle to find
parts.ask: The speed at B is 5 m/s: use the work-energy principle to find U
parts.ms: M1 work-energy equation, all terms (M0 if not work-energy), condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion; A1ft at most one error; A1ft ½(3)U² − (a) − 3g(4 sin α) = ½(3)(25); A1 9.79 or 9.8 (MS p.14)

parts.ask: P leaves the ramp at B and moves freely under gravity to the ground at C: find the horizontal distance from B to C
parts.ms: M1 suvat with u = 5 for t; A1 −4 sin α = (5 sin α)t − ½gt²; A1 t = 0.4597…; M1 horizontal distance with u = 5; A1ft (5 cos α)t = (30/√37)t; A1 2.27 or 2.3. Alt: quadratic in the horizontal distance (MS p.14)

parts.ms: M1 moments about the y-axis (x-direction), all terms, dimensionally consistent, condone m missing throughout; A1* given answer from 2m(−2) + 3m(2) + 4m(3k) = 9m x̄ (MS p.7)
parts.er: Most formed the relevant equation and derived the result (ER p.3)

parts.ask: The centre of mass lies on the line x + 2y = 3: find k
parts.ms: M1 moments for ȳ (all terms); A1 ȳ = (1 + 4k)/9; DM1 substitute their x̄, ȳ into x + 2y = 3 and solve (dependent on both M marks); A1 23/20 cao (MS p.7)
parts.er: Common errors were slips in forming/solving the equation in k, especially after rearranging before substituting; a few equated the line gradient to the ratio of coordinates; a few never found ȳ (ER pp.3–4)

parts.ask: Car of mass 900 kg moving DOWN a road inclined at α (sin α = 1/12); engine works at 15 kW, resistance 400 N: find the acceleration when the speed is 16 m/s
parts.ms: M1 use of P = Fv (F = 15000/16 = 937.5), condone 15 for 15000; M1 equation of motion, all terms, condone sign errors and sin/cos confusion; A1 at most one error; A1 correct: 15000/16 + 900g(1/12) − 400 = 900a; A1 1.41 or 1.4 (MS p.8)
parts.er: Well understood; main errors were signs, usually resistance in the wrong direction; several lost the final mark by not giving 2 or 3 s.f. after using g = 9.8 (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Particle of mass 0.2 kg with velocity (4i − 3j) m/s receives impulse λ(i + j) N s; its speed afterwards is 7 m/s: find the possible values of λ
parts.ms: M1 I = mv − mu (subtraction, dimensionally correct; using 7 as the velocity is M0 unless recovered); A1 0.2(v − (4i − 3j)) = λ(i + j); M1 Pythagoras with 49 for speed²; A1 correct equation; DM1 form and solve a quadratic, e.g. (5λ + 4)² + (5λ − 3)² = 49; A1 both values. Special case: treating 7 as a vector scores at most M1A0M1A0DM1A0 if they recover. Alt: vector triangle + cosine rule (MS p.9)
parts.er: Most knew impulse = change in momentum and speed = magnitude of velocity; the majority of errors came from treating the speed 7 as a vector — "it is not correct to equate a scalar quantity to a vector quantity" (ER pp.3–4)

parts.ask: v = √(5 − t) i + (t² + 2t − 3) j for 0 ≤ t < 5; at t = λ P moves parallel to i: find the acceleration of P at t = λ
parts.ms: M1 set j-component = 0 and solve (λ² + 2λ − 3 = 0); A1 λ = 1 only; M1 differentiate both components, powers going down; A1 a = −1/(2√(5 − t)) i + (2t + 2) j; A1 −¼ i + 4j, ISW if magnitude found (MS p.10)
parts.er: High scoring; some found the magnitude, not asked for (time wasted, no penalty if the vector was stated); a minority set the i-component to zero or set the j-component of a to zero; chain-rule errors differentiating √(5 − t) (ER pp.3–4)

parts.ask: Given r = (−2i + j) m at t = 1, find the position vector at t = T (1 ≤ T < 5) in terms of T
parts.ms: M1 integrate both components, powers going up (M0 if a component assumed zero); A1 at most one error; A1 correct, constants optional; DM1 use t = 1, r = −2i + j to find the constants; A1 any equivalent vector (MS p.10)
parts.er: Integrating √(5 − t) caused problems; sign slips; some thought the j-component would be zero; some ignored the constant of integration or just added −2i + j to their answer (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Uniform rod AB, length 8a, weight W, hinged at A to the ground, rests against a fixed smooth hemisphere (radius 2a, centre D) touching at C with AC = 5a: show AD = √29 a
parts.ms: B1* Pythagoras √((2a)² + (5a)²) = √29 a, with a on both sides (MS p.11)
parts.er: Almost all gave a correct explanation (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Show the normal reaction at C has magnitude 4W/√29
parts.ms: M1 M(A): W·4a cos θ = N·5a, dimensionally correct, condone sin/cos confusion; A1 with cos θ = 5/√29 substituted; A1* given answer from correct working (MS p.11)
parts.er: Many fully correct; several attempts to "fiddle" working to reach the given answer — show sufficient working and obtain the answer exactly as given (ER p.4)

parts.ask: The resultant force at A has magnitude kW at angle α to the ground: find (i) the exact value of k, (ii) the exact value of tan α
parts.ms: M1A1 resolve vertically: V + N cos θ = W (V = 9W/29); M1A1 resolve horizontally: H = N sin θ = 8W/29; DM1 Pythagoras for k; A1 √145/29, ISW, but 0.415 with no exact answer seen is A0; DM1 trig for tan α; A1 9/8 (not including W). Alt: resolve parallel/perpendicular to the rod, or M(C) (MS pp.11–12)
parts.er: Most resolved horizontally and vertically; confusion from unlabelled diagrams; some had a correct pair of equations but could not solve them; some gave kW rather than k (ER pp.3–4)

parts.ask: L-shaped uniform lamina PQRSTUV made of two identical rectangles (PQ = RS = 2a, PV = QR = ka): show its centre of mass is (6 + k)a/4 from PV
parts.ms: M1 moments about PV (parallel axis allowed), dimensionally consistent; A1 a·2ka² + (2a + ½ka)·2ka² = x̄(4ka²); A1* given answer (MS p.13)
parts.er: Most took moments about PV as the question hints; splitting the shape differently or using a large rectangle minus a piece made extra, more complex work (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Lamina freely suspended from P hangs with PR at α to the downward vertical, tan α = 7/15: find k
parts.ms: M1 moments about PR (or another horizontal axis); A1 correct equation; A1 distance from PR = (k + 2)a/4; M1 use the given ratio (reciprocal allowed); A1 7/15 = ((k + 2)a/4)/((6 + k)a/4); A1 3/2 (MS p.13)
parts.er: Marking the centre of mass and the line from P helped; those using UV as axis made wrong assumptions about vertical distances; few used the correct (a − ka) below UV for QRST (ER p.5)

parts.ask: A (mass m, speed 3u) collides directly with B (mass 2m, speed u) moving the same way; coefficient e: (i) show B's speed after is (5 + 2e)u/3, (ii) find A's speed after
parts.ms: M1 CLM, condone sign errors; A1 3mu + 2mu = mv_A + 2mv_B; M1 NEL the right way round; A1 v_B − v_A = e(3u − u), signs consistent; DM1 solve; A1* given v_B; A1 v_A = (5 − 4e)u/3, must be positive (MS p.14)
parts.er: Most errors were signs; those who assumed A reversed often did not notice their velocity was negative and lost the final mark since a positive speed was required (ER pp.3, 5)

parts.ask: B then hits a smooth fixed wall (e = 1/3) and rebounds; the first A–B collision is distance d from the wall; with e = 1/2, find the time T between the two A–B collisions in terms of d and u
parts.ms: B1 time for B to reach the wall d/(2u); B1 B's rebound speed (1/3)(5 + 2e)u/3 = 2u/3; M1 distance A travels meanwhile (d/2) using their v_A = u; M1 closing-gap equation with relative speeds; A1 d/2 = ut + 2ut/3 ⇒ t = 3d/(10u); A1 total d/(2u) + 3d/(10u) = 4d/(5u) (MS p.14)
parts.er: Many solutions lacked a clear strategy; the wall-time B1 was awarded less often than the rebound-speed B1; some never substituted e, making the algebra very complicated (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Particle of mass 0.3 kg projected up a rough ramp AB (15 m, tan α = 7/24, μ = 1/5), reaching B with velocity (24i + 7j) m/s: find the work done against friction from A to B
parts.er: Errors: sin/cos confusion, omitting g from the reaction, not giving 2 or 3 s.f. (ER p.5)

parts.command: Use the work-energy principle to find
parts.ask: Use the work-energy principle to find U
parts.ms: M1 work-energy equation, all terms, condone sign errors; A1ft at most one error; A1ft ½(0.3)U² = ½(0.3)(25²) + (a) + 0.3g(15 sin α); A1 27.6 or 28 (MS p.15)
parts.er: Main errors were signs; some omitted the KE at the top of the ramp or the work against friction; rounding errors (ER p.6)

parts.ask: P leaves the ramp at B and moves freely under gravity to the ground at C: find the time from B to C
parts.ms: M1 complete suvat method for t; A1ft −15 sin α (= −4.2) = 7t − ½gt²; A1 1.88 or 1.9; the exact form (5 + √67)/7 is A0 (MS p.15)
parts.er: Sign errors, wrong vertical distance, confusing U with the speed at B, mixing horizontal and vertical components (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Just before hitting the ground P moves downwards at θ° to the horizontal: find θ
parts.ms: M1 vertical component at C (7 − 9.8t ≈ −11.46) or speed by energy (v ≈ 26.59); A1ft (7√67/5 condoned for the vertical component); M1 tan θ = vertical/24 or cos θ = 24/speed; A1 25.5 or 26 (MS p.15)
parts.er: Some confused energy conservation with v² = u² + 2as using u = 25; confusion between horizontal and vertical components in the trig (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Truck (1500 kg) on a level road, engine at 30 kW, constant resistance R N; acceleration 0.6 m/s² at 20 m/s: find R
parts.ms: M1 equation of motion F − R = 1500a; A1 correct in F or P; M1 30000/20 − R = 1500 × 0.6 (zeros error condoned for M); A1 600 (MS p.7)
parts.er: Most scored full marks; the most common error was 30 for 30000 (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Later it moves up a road inclined at α (sin α = 1/8), non-gravitational resistance 500 N, engine at 30 kW; its deceleration is 0.2 m/s² when the speed is V: find V
parts.ms: M1 equation of motion with all terms; A1 at most one error, F substituted; A1 30000/V − 1500g/8 − 500 = −1500 × 0.2; A1 14.7. If F is never substituted, A0A0 (MS p.7)
parts.er: More challenging; most common error was treating 0.2 as an acceleration; also sign errors and missing terms (ER p.3)

parts.ask: P (0.5 kg) moving with velocity (5i + 3j) m/s receives impulse (−2i + λj) N s; its velocity becomes (xi + yj) and its KE increases by 22 J: find the possible values of λ
parts.final_form: λ = 4 or λ = −7 (both, no errors seen)
parts.ms: M1 change-in-KE equation (subtracting); A1 ½·0.5(x² + y² − 34) = 22 (x² + y² = 122); M1 impulse-momentum; A1 0.5(xi + yj) − 0.5(5i + 3j) = −2i + λj (x = 1, y = 2λ + 3); DM1 quadratic in λ, 1 + (2λ + 3)² = 122; DM1 solve for two values; A1 4 or −7 (watch for x = −1). ePEN shows M1A1A1 for the last three but they are marked DM1DM1A1 (MS p.7)
parts.er: Most formed the impulse-momentum equation correctly (a few subtracted the wrong way); several took 22 J as the final KE, used ½m(v − u)², or omitted squares of speeds; many overlooked one of the two solutions (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Rectangle ABDE (AB = 8a, BD = 6a) with isosceles triangle BCD (base BD = 6a, height 6a) removed to form template ABCDE: show its centre of mass is 14a/5 from AE
parts.final_form: printed result 14a/5, with correct use of a
parts.ms: B1 mass ratios 48a² : 18a² : 30a²; B1 distances from AE 4a and 8a − 2a = 6a; M1 moments about AE (or parallel axis); A1 48a²·4a − 18a²·6a = 30a²·x̄; A1* 84a/30 = 14a/5. Moments about BD giving 5.2a allows B1B1M1A1A0 (MS p.8)
parts.er: Mostly correct; rectangle minus triangle was most concise; errors were a wrong triangle centre of mass or inconsistent use of a; rewrite rather than overwrite corrected working (ER p.4)

parts.ask: The template is freely suspended from A and hangs with AB at θ° to the downward vertical: find θ to the nearest whole number
parts.final_form: θ = 47 (nearest degree; 47.0 or radians not accepted)
parts.ms: M1 trig for a relevant angle; A1 tan θ = 3a/2.8a; A1 47. Going on to 90 − 47 = 43 is M1A0A0 (do not ISW); 0.82 rad scores M1A1A0 (MS p.8)
parts.er: Many fully correct; some found 47 and then concluded 43; 47.0 or a radian answer was not accepted since a whole number of degrees was asked (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Particle Q (1.5 kg) on a smooth horizontal plane under a single force F; v = (3t² + 2t)i + (t³ + kt)j for t ≥ 0; at t = 2 Q moves in the direction of i + j: show k = 4
parts.final_form: printed result k = 4 (verification allowed with a clear conclusion)
parts.ms: M1 t = 2 with equal components: 12 + 4 = 8 + 2k; A1* (MS p.9)
parts.er: Mostly correct, linking direction of motion to velocity; a few algebra/arithmetic slips. Across the question a significant number scored nothing by trying suvat (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Find the magnitude of F when t = 2
parts.ms: M1 a = dv/dt; A1 a = (6t + 2)i + (3t² + 4)j; DM1 F = ma with Pythagoras, 1.5√(14² + 16²); A1 3√113 (MS p.9)
parts.er: Mostly well structured; slips in differentiation/arithmetic; some found a but not F, or F as a vector without its magnitude (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Given r = 3i + 4j at t = 0, find r when t = 2
parts.ms: M1 r = ∫v dt; A1 (t³ + t²)i + (t⁴/4 + 2t²)j (+ constants); DM1 use r(0) = 3i + 4j and t = 2 (using −3i − 4j is M0); A1 15i + 16j (MS p.9)
parts.er: Some integration slips but most used the initial position correctly; a minority used suvat inappropriately (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Package (1.5 kg) projected up a rough ramp (tan θ = 5/12) from A, first coming to rest at B (AB = 2.5 m); μ = 2/7: find the work done against friction from A to B
parts.ms: M1 F_max = (2/7)(1.5g cos θ) (3.87…); M1 WD = 2.5F_max (M0 if GPE included); A1 9.69 (MS p.10)
parts.er: Key steps were friction then work done; several used sine instead of cosine, some ignored μ; giving total work against weight and friction scored at most 1 (ER p.4)

parts.command: Use the work-energy principle to find
parts.ask: Use the work-energy principle to find U, the projection speed at A
parts.ms: M1 work-energy equation, all terms (if (a) included GPE it must be used as total work here); A1ft at most one error; A1ft ½·1.5U² = WD + 1.5 × 9.8 × 2.5 sin θ; A1 5.64 (MS p.10)
parts.er: Other methods scored nothing; errors were wrong accuracy, sign errors, double-counting GPE and omitting a term (ER p.4)

parts.command: Use the work-energy principle to find
parts.ask: The package then slides back from rest at B: use the work-energy principle to find its speed when it returns to A
parts.ms: M1 work-energy for A to A (½·1.5v² = ½·1.5U² − 2WD) or B to A (½·1.5v² = 1.5 × 9.8 × 2.5 sin θ − WD); A1ft; A1 2.43 (MS p.10)
parts.er: Work-energy required; sign errors in (b) were often repeated; most considered B to A, a few A to A (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Uniform pole AB (50 N, 6 m) hinged at A to a vertical wall, particle W N at B, held at 60° to the wall by a light rod from C on the pole (AC = 4 m) to D on the wall below A (AD = 4 m); thrust in the rod is 60√3 N: show W = 15
parts.ms: M1 moments about A (or equivalent), all terms (sin/cos and sign condoned); A1 at most one error; A1 50 × 3 cos 30° + W × 6 cos 30° = 60√3 × 4 sin 30°; A1* (MS p.11)
parts.er: Most took moments about A; several claimed the answer from an incorrect equation; most errors were handling the thrust and sine/cosine confusion (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Find the magnitude of the resultant force acting on the pole at A
parts.ms: M1 A1 first equation, e.g. vertical V + 50 + 15 = T cos 30° (V = 25); M1 A1 second, e.g. horizontal H = T cos 60° = 30√3; DM1 R = √(25² + (30√3)²); A1 5√133. Alt: resolve along/perpendicular to the pole, a second moments equation, or a vector triangle with the cosine rule (MS p.11)
parts.er: Resolving horizontally and vertically was most common and usually successful; resolving along/perpendicular to the pole or a second moments equation often mishandled the force at A (ER p.5)

parts.ask: P (3m, speed 2u) and Q (km, speed 3u) move towards each other and collide; afterwards P has speed u (direction unchanged) and Q speed v: show v = (3 − 3k)u/k
parts.final_form: printed result v = (3 − 3k)u/k from full working
parts.ms: M1 CLM (or equal and opposite impulses), all terms; A1 6mu − 3kmu = 3mu + kmv; A1* (MS p.12)
parts.er: Many fully correct; errors came from misreading the directions before and after; most did not use the impact law here, following the structure (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Find, in terms of m and u, the magnitude of the impulse received by Q
parts.ms: M1 impulse = change in momentum for either particle; A1 |I_P| = |3mu − 3m·2u| = 3mu (MS p.12)
parts.er: Mostly correct; using P was much simpler; the magnitude was required (ER p.5)

parts.ask: The coefficient of restitution is e; given v ≠ u, find the range of possible values of k
parts.ms: M1 impact law; A1 (v − u)/(5u) = e or ((3 − 3k)/k)u − u = 5ue; M1 v > u (or e > 0) gives an inequality; M1 e ≤ 1 gives an inequality; A1 (3 − 3k)/k > 1 and 3 − 3k ≤ 6k, so 1/3 ≤ k < 3/4 (MS p.12)
parts.er: Most stated the impact law and found e in terms of k, then needed 0 ≤ e ≤ 1; most got one inequality but few understood the significance of v ≠ u (ER p.5)

parts.ask: P projected from O with speed u at α above the horizontal; at horizontal distance x it is y above O: show y = x tan α − (gx²/2u²)(1 + tan²α)
parts.final_form: printed result, with the final step justified (1/cos²α = 1 + tan²α must be explained)
parts.ms: M1 A1 x = u cos α·t; M1 A1 y = u sin α·t − ½gt²; DM1 eliminate t; A1* given answer with evidence for sec²α = 1 + tan²α (MS p.13)
parts.er: Standard bookwork; some sign errors in the vertical equation; some did not explain the last step — 1/cos²α = 1 + tan²α should be explained (ER p.5)

parts.command: Use the principle of conservation of mechanical energy to find
parts.ask: Ball projected from A (20 m vertically above B on horizontal ground) with speed U at θ° above the horizontal lands at C (BC = 30 m) at 25 m/s: use conservation of mechanical energy to find U
parts.ms: M1 energy equation, all terms; A1 ½m·25² = ½mU² + mg × 20; A1 15.3 (MS p.13)
parts.er: Those who used energy as instructed usually succeeded; some over-specified; several tried suvat with U and 25 (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Find the value of θ
parts.ms: M1 use (a) (or first principles) with x = 30, y = −20 for an equation in tan θ; A1ft 18.9 tan²θ − 30 tan θ − 1.07 = 0 or equivalent (4410/233 tan²θ − 30 tan θ − 250/233 = 0), follow their U; A1 58.3 (MS p.13)
parts.er: Using (a) was most efficient; first-principles attempts rarely reached an equation in tan θ; the commonest error was the sign of the vertical displacement (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Particle P (0.3 kg) moving at 5i m/s receives impulse I; afterwards its velocity is (7i + 7j) m/s: find |I|
parts.ms: M1 I = mv − mu, must subtract (wrong order condoned); A1 0.3((7i + 7j) − 5i) = 0.6i + 2.1j; M1 Pythagoras; A1 2.18 (MS p.7)
parts.er: Many fully correct; mu − mv accepted since a magnitude is asked; some stopped at 0.6i + 2.1j without Pythagoras; a minority found |7i + 7j| first (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Find the angle between I and the direction of motion of P before the impulse
parts.final_form: 74.1° (74 or better; 74.0546…; 286 or 1.29 rad also accepted)
parts.ms: M1 trig or scalar product for a relevant angle with their I; A1 tan θ = 2.1/0.6 (or cos θ = 2/√53 type) with no other angle involved; A1 74.1 (MS p.7)
parts.er: Mostly correct with tan θ = 2.1/0.6; some started with 0.6/2.1 but did not go on to the required angle; some used the wrong velocity; a few used the scalar product (ER p.4)

parts.ask: v = (4t² − 5t)i + (−10t − 12)j for t ≥ 0 on a smooth horizontal plane (show all stages; no calculator technology); r = 2i + 6j at t = 0: find r when t = 2
parts.final_form: r = (8/3)i − 38j (2.7 or better for 8/3); ISW if magnitude found
parts.ms: M1 r = ∫v dt, powers up by 1 (one slip allowed); A1 r = ((4/3)t³ − (5/2)t² + A)i + (−5t² − 12t + B)j; M1 use r(0) = 2i + 6j and t = 2; A1 (8/3)i − 38j (MS p.8)
parts.er: Confident topic, many fully correct; some slips substituting t = 2, some forgot the boundary condition for the constants, and simplification errors after correct work (ER p.4)

parts.ask: When t = T, P moves in the direction of i − 2j: find T
parts.ms: M1 form an equation in T from the direction (−2 on the wrong side condoned); A1 −2(4T² − 5T) = −10T − 12 (8T² − 20T − 12 = 0); A1 3 (MS p.8)
parts.er: Common errors: −2 on the wrong side, or equating v to i − 2j; introducing a ratio variable worked but took longer (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Find the exact magnitude of the acceleration when t = 2.5
parts.final_form: √325 = 5√13 m s⁻², exact (decimals after the exact value ignored)
parts.ms: M1 a = dv/dt = (8t − 5)i − 10j; M1 Pythagoras at t = 2.5; A1 5√13 (MS p.8)
parts.er: Many fully correct; decimal-only answers lost the final mark as exact was required; some did 15² − 10² instead of 15² + 10² (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Uniform isosceles triangular lamina ABC (height 9y, base BC = 6x, AB = AC); P on AC and Q on AB with AP : PC = AQ : QB = 2 : 1; the lamina is folded along PQ to form F: show the centre of mass of F is d = 16y/9 from PQ
parts.final_form: printed result d = 16y/9 from fully correct working
parts.ms: B1 distances from PQ for a complete dissection (e.g. large triangle 0, folded small triangle −2y and +2y); B1 mass ratios (27xy, 12xy, 12xy, 27xy); M1 moments about PQ, all non-zero terms; A1 27xy·0 − 12xy(−2y) + 12xy(2y) = 27xy·d; A1* 48y/27 = 16y/9. A false trapezium centre of mass scores 0/5; for PQBC the correct distance is 8y/5 (MS p.9)
parts.er: By far the least successful question; dozens of convoluted, poorly explained dissections; moments about PQ were sensible; many did not see it as just two triangles; trapezium users often wrongly asserted its centre of mass was 1.5y from PQ (ER p.4)

parts.ask: F is suspended from P and hangs freely with PQ at α to the downward vertical, tan α = 64/81: find x in terms of y
parts.ms: M1 trig for a relevant angle (α or 90° − α); A1 tan α = (16y/9)/(2x) = 64/81; A1 9y/8 (MS p.10)
parts.er: Many who failed (a) used the given result to score full marks; most used symmetry for the distance from P, some used a second moments equation; 3x instead of 2x was a common error (ER p.5)

parts.ask: P (3m, speed u) and Q (5m, speed ku) move towards each other and collide; afterwards P has speed 2v and Q speed v, both reversed; P receives an impulse of magnitude 15mv: show u = 3v
parts.ms: M1 impulse-momentum for P with 3m (subtraction evident); A1 15mv = 3m(2v − (−u)); A1* 9mv = 3mu. Alt: impulse on Q gives k = 2v/u, then CLM (MS p.11)
parts.er: The impulse must be used; starting from the impulse on P was quickest; starting with Q needed a second equation to eliminate k; CLM alone scored nothing; sign errors, then candidates went on to "fudge" the given answer (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Find k
parts.ms: M1 impulse-momentum for Q or CLM; A1 15mv = 5m(v − (−ku)) or 3mu − 5mku = 5mv − 6mv; A1 2/3 (MS p.11)
parts.er: Most used CLM, but a second use of the impulse was common; sign errors were common (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Find the coefficient of restitution e
parts.ms: M1 impact law the right way round; A1ft 2v + v = e(u + ku) = e·5v, follow their k; A1 3/5 (MS p.11)
parts.er: Mostly correct for their k; a minority used the law the wrong way round; recalling it as a formula rather than separation/approach speeds led to sign errors (ER p.5)

parts.ask: The total KE lost in the collision is λmv²: find λ
parts.ms: M1 change in KE with all four terms and correct masses (gain allowed); A1 ½·3m(u² − (2v)²) + ½·5m((ku)² − v²); A1 15 (MS pp.11–12)
parts.er: Most scored the method mark but slipped substituting/simplifying; some used ½m(v − u)², one particle only, or m instead of 3m and 5m (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Uniform beam AB (15 kg, 6 m) at 75° to the ground, A on rough ground, B against a rough vertical wall (μ_wall = 0.2), in limiting equilibrium: find the normal reaction at B
parts.final_form: R_B = 19 N or 18.7 N (2 or 3 s.f.)
parts.ms: M1 moments about A, all terms; A1 at most one error; A1 15g·3 cos 75° = F_B·6 cos 75° + R_B·6 sin 75°; M1 use F_B = 0.2R_B in the moments equation; A1 18.7 (MS p.13)
parts.er: Most took moments about A; errors were sin/cos confusion and omitting the wall friction or giving it the wrong direction; a few took the reaction perpendicular to the beam; 2 or 3 s.f. needed (ER p.5)

parts.ask: The coefficient of friction at the ground is μ: find μ
parts.final_form: μ = 0.13 or better (0.1304784…; 0.131 from premature rounding loses the mark)
parts.ms: M1 A1 resolve horizontally F_A = R_B; M1 A1 resolve vertically R_A + F_B = 15g (R_A = 143.26…); DM1 F_A = μR_A; A1 0.130. Alt: moments about B (MS p.13)
parts.er: Resolving horizontally and vertically then F = μR was most straightforward; a wrong (a) could score all but the last mark; moments about B or resolving along the beam was less successful; 0.131 from premature approximation was common (ER pp.5–6)

parts.ask: Van (900 kg) on a level road, resistance 600 N, engine at 24 kW; acceleration 2 m/s² when the speed is V: find V
parts.ms: M1 equation of motion; A1 F − 600 = 900 × 2; M1 F = 24000/V; A1 10 (MS p.14)
parts.er: Almost all correct (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Later the van tows a trailer (700 kg) by a light towbar up a road inclined at θ (sin θ = 1/14); non-gravitational resistances 600 N and 550 N; engine at 24 kW: find the acceleration at 8 m/s
parts.ms: M1 equation of motion for the system (separate equations must eliminate T); A1 at most one error; A1 24000/8 − 1600g sin θ − 1150 = 1600a; A1 0.456. Missing g is an accuracy error (MS p.14)
parts.er: Many correct; common errors were omitting g from weight components or not resolving them; 73/160 lost the final mark (ER p.6)

parts.command: Use the work-energy principle to find
parts.ask: At 9 m/s the towbar breaks; the trailer moves d m up the road to instantaneous rest: use the work-energy principle to find d
parts.ms: M1 work-energy for the trailer only (mass 700, resistance 550), no duplication; A1 at most one error; A1 ½·700·9² = 550d + 700g·d sin θ; A1 27.3 (MS p.14)
parts.er: More challenging; suvat solutions scored nothing; errors were omitting work against resistance, counting GPE and work against gravity separately, 900 or 1600 kg for the mass, and omitting d from the resistance work (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Ball projected from A, 20 m above horizontal ground, with velocity (3i + 2j) m/s, landing at B: by considering energy, find its speed just before hitting the ground
parts.final_form: 20 or 20.1 m/s (2 or 3 s.f. only; not 9√5)
parts.ms: M1 energy equation (required); A1 ½mv² = ½m(9 + 4) + mg × 20; A1 20.1 (MS p.15)
parts.er: Most used energy as told; suvat scored nothing; a surd answer lost the final mark (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Find the direction of motion of the ball just before it hits the ground
parts.final_form: 81° (81.4°) below the horizontal, stated clearly (or vector 3i − 19.9j)
parts.ms: M1 complete method for a relevant angle; A1ft cos θ = 3/their (a); A1 81.4 below the horizontal, stated in words or on a diagram. Alt: vertical component √(their (a)² − 9) giving 3i − 19.9j (MS p.15)
parts.er: Various approaches; simplest used the horizontal component with (a); a statement of where the angle is measured was required; vector answers were usually correct (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Find the time taken from A to B
parts.ms: M1 suvat equation in t; A1 −20 = 2t − ½gt²; A1 2.23 (MS p.15)
parts.er: Many correct; some split at the greatest height; some confused the speed with the vertical component (ER p.6)

parts.ask: When the direction of motion is perpendicular to 3i + 2j the ball is h m above the ground: find h
parts.ms: B1 velocity 3i − λj (horizontal component unchanged); M1 (3i + 2j)·(3i − λj) = 0; A1 v = 3i − 4.5j; dM1 suvat or energy for the vertical distance (3i − 2j is not equivalent); A1 4.5² = 2² + 2gs or energy equation; A1 h = 20 − s = 19.2 (MS p.15)
parts.er: More challenging; scalar product users were usually successful; some took 3i − 2j as perpendicular, or did not keep the horizontal component; angle methods confused; a few did not subtract from 20 (ER p.7)

parts.ask: r = (t⁴ − 8t²)i + (6t² − 2t^{3/2})j for t > 0: find the velocity of P when it moves parallel to j
parts.final_form: vector: (24 − 3√2)j m/s (accept 20j or better; 19.757…j); must be a vector
parts.ms: M1 differentiate both components (a power down in each); A1 v = (4t³ − 16t)i + (12t − 3t^{1/2})j; DM1 i-component = 0, solve (t = 2); A1 (24 − 3√2)j. Column vectors accepted (MS p.7)
parts.er: Many fully correct; a few integrated; several used the wrong component or a component of r; the answer must be a vector but several omitted j (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Find the acceleration of P when t = 4
parts.final_form: vector: 176i + (45/4)j m s⁻² (accept 180i + 11j or better); ISW
parts.ms: M1 differentiate their vector v; A1 a = (12t² − 16)i + (12 − (3/2)t^{−1/2})j; A1 176i + 45/4 j (MS p.7)
parts.er: Answered well; errors were slips substituting t; several wasted time finding the magnitude, which was not asked (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Template of three coplanar squares: PQUY (side 4a), RSTU and VWXY (side 2a each) with double the mass per unit area of PQUY: show the centre of mass is d = 5a/2 from PX
parts.final_form: printed result, ending "d = 5a/2" with at least one simplification step
parts.ms: B1 mass ratios 16a² : 8a² : 8a² (2 : 1 : 1); B1 distances from PX 2a, 5a, a; M1 moments about PX or a parallel axis (vector form allowed); A1 16a²·2a + 8a²·5a + 8a²·a = 32a²·d; A1* 80a = 32d (MS p.8)
parts.er: Well understood; several conclusions never mentioned d; some lacked working for the given answer; a appeared and disappeared; a minority ignored the different densities; vector approaches found both coordinates at once (ER pp.3–4)

parts.ask: The template is freely pivoted about Q and hangs in equilibrium with PQ at θ to the downward vertical: find tan θ
parts.ms: M1 moments about PQ (or a parallel axis); A1ft at most one error; A1 16a²·2a + 8a²·3a + 8a²·5a = 32a²·h; A1 h = 3a from PQ; M1 trig for a relevant angle, e.g. tan θ = 3a/(4a − 5a/2); A1 2. Working must be seen or used in (b) (MS p.8)
parts.er: Most started by finding the horizontal distance; a few who had it in (a) did not see its relevance; some stated θ without ever stating tan θ and lost the final mark (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Template of mass M, still pivoted at Q, held with PQ vertical by a horizontal force F at X in its plane: find F in terms of M and g
parts.ms: M1 complete method, e.g. moments about Q; A1 3a·Mg = 4a·F (a missing throughout condoned); A1 3Mg/4 (MS p.8)
parts.er: Least successful part; most took moments about Q but with wrong distances, or tried to resolve F and Mg when the distances were already perpendicular to the forces (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Particle Q (0.25 kg) moving at 8 m/s receives an impulse of magnitude I N s parallel to the surface at 60° to its original direction; its speed afterwards is 12 m/s and its direction turns through α°: find I
parts.ms: M1 impulse-momentum equation; A1 one correct component, e.g. I cos 60° = ¼(12 cos α − 8); M1 second equation; A1 I sin 60° = ¼(12 sin α); DM1 eliminate α: 36 = (I + 4)² + 3I² (4I² + 8I − 20 = 0); A1 √6 − 1. Alt: vector triangle with 120° and cosine rule 4 + I² − 4I cos 120° = 9 (MS p.9)
parts.er: Most resolved parallel and perpendicular to the initial direction; sine/cosine confusion; missing brackets (8 written for 0.25 × 8) cost four marks; eliminating α to get a quadratic in I was the more successful route; the vector triangle with the cosine rule was very effective (ER p.4)

parts.ask: P projected from A on horizontal ground with velocity (4i + 4j) m/s lands at B; at time T₁ it is at its highest point: find T₁
parts.final_form: T₁ = 0.408 or 0.41 (3 or 2 s.f. only; not 20/49)
parts.er: Mostly successful; common errors were leaving a fraction or giving more than 3 s.f. (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Q is projected from A at t = 0 with velocity (5i + 7j) m/s: find the vertical distance between Q and P at time T₁, to 2 significant figures
parts.ms: M1 suvat with initial vertical components 7 and 4; A1 h = (7T₁ − ½gT₁²) − (4T₁ − ½gT₁²) = 3T₁; A1ft 1.2 (MS p.10)
parts.er: Some found the distance between the particles or the difference of their greatest heights; some swapped Q's components; many ignored the 2 s.f. instruction (ER p.4)

parts.ask: When P reaches B, Q is moving at α° below the horizontal: find α
parts.ms: B1 time to B = 2T₁ (0.816…); M1 Q's vertical velocity 7 − g(2T₁) = −1 (must use 7); M1 tan α = 1/5 with their values; A1 11. Using T₁ instead of 2T₁ scores B0M0M1A0 (MS p.10)
parts.er: Most knew the time was 2T₁; confusion over whether Q's initial vertical component was 5 or 7; some used 4 instead of 5 horizontally; premature rounding spoiled the angle; a minority used distances instead of velocities (ER p.5)

parts.ask: At time T₂ the direction of motion of Q is perpendicular to its initial direction: find T₂
parts.ms: M1 perpendicular gradients/scalar product, e.g. (5, 7)·(5, 7 − gT₂) = 0; A1 −25/7 = 7 − gT₂; A1 1.08 (MS p.10)
parts.er: Most challenging part, often not attempted; working with velocity vectors helped; sign errors, and some used a distance formula instead of velocity (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Cyclist and cycle (80 kg) on a level road working at 500 W, resistance 60 N: find the acceleration when the speed is 6 m/s
parts.ms: M1 F = 500/6; M1 equation of motion, no extras; A1 F − 60 = 80a; A1 7/24 (MS p.11)
parts.er: Most set up the equation of motion with P = Fv; a few omitted the 60 N or slipped in arithmetic (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Next day she rides 20 km from A (500 m above sea level) to B (800 m), starting from rest and reaching 8 m/s, resistance 60 N: find the total work done by the cyclist
parts.final_form: 1440 kJ or 1400 kJ (3 or 2 s.f.; 1437760 J before rounding; joules accepted)
parts.ms: B1 one correct term (KE gain ½·80·8² = 2560 J or GPE gain 80 × 9.8 × 300 = 235200 J); B1 a second; M1 combined work-energy expression with work against resistance 20000 × 60, no double counting (suvat with F = ma is M0A0A0); A1 correct expression; A1 1440 kJ (MS p.11)
parts.er: Many did not use work and energy; common errors were KE change between the two days, omitting work against resistance, double-counting the PE gain, and too many significant figures (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Later she rides up a road inclined at α (sin α = 1/20) at a constant 7 m/s working at P watts, resistance 60 N: find P
parts.final_form: P = 694 or 690 (3 or 2 s.f. only; 694.4 loses the final mark)
parts.ms: M1 equation of motion with zero acceleration; A1 at most one error; A1 P/7 − 60 − 80g/20 = 0; A1 694 (MS p.11)
parts.er: Many scored the first three marks; errors were sin/cos confusion, signs and missing g; the most common error was giving 694.4 (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Uniform rod AB (8a, weight W) hinged at A to a vertical wall, particle W/4 at B; string of length 5a from C on the rod (AC = 5a) to D on the wall above A (AD = 5a): show the tension is T = 6W/5
parts.final_form: printed result, with cancelling or simplification shown
parts.ms: M1 moments about A with resolved terms (M0 with no resolving); A1 4a cos 30°·W + 8a cos 30°·(W/4) = 5a cos 30°·T; A1* 6W = 5T (MS p.12). Triangle ACD is equilateral, so the rod is at 60° to the wall.
parts.er: Most formed a dimensionally correct moments equation; sin/cos confusions sometimes cancelled out; many showed no working from the correct equation to the given answer; a few did not find the angle in the triangle (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Find, in terms of W, the magnitude of the force exerted on the rod by the hinge at A
parts.ms: M1 A1 first equation, e.g. H = T cos 30° = 3√3W/5; M1 A1 second, e.g. V + T cos 60° = W + W/4, V = 13W/20; DM1 R = √(H² + V²); A1 √601 W/20. Alternatives: moments about B or C, resolving parallel/perpendicular to the rod (MS p.12)
parts.er: Most resolved horizontally and vertically then used Pythagoras; many left exact answers; some had two correct equations but went no further; alternative methods often missed a component of the hinge force; a few included a reaction at D (ER p.5)

parts.ask: P (4m, speed 2u) and Q (2m, speed 3u) move towards each other and collide; both are reversed (speeds x and y); total KE after is half the KE before: show y = 8u/3
parts.final_form: printed result y = 8u/3, with working to the quadratic shown
parts.ms: M1 CLM; A1 8mu − 6mu = 2my − 4mx (u = y − 2x); M1 KE equation with correct pairings and the ½ applied; A1 2mx² + my² = ½(2m·4u² + m·9u²); DM1 eliminate x: 17u² = 2y² + (y − u)², 3y² − 2uy − 16u² = 0; A1* (3y − 8u)(y + 2u) = 0 (MS p.13)
parts.er: CLM almost always formed; directions often overlooked; KE terms subtracted instead of added, 2 on the wrong side, arithmetic slips; some never combined the equations, and many just stated the given answer ("wishful thinking") (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Find the coefficient of restitution e between P and Q
parts.ms: M1 impact law the right way round, x + y = 5ue; A1 x = 5u/6 so e = (5u/6 + 8u/3)/(5u); A1 7/10 (MS p.13)
parts.er: Mostly correct using CLM and the given y; some sign errors, very few used the law the wrong way round (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Q then hits a smooth fixed wall perpendicular to its motion (coefficient f) and rebounds; given there is no second collision between P and Q, find the range of f
parts.ms: B1 Q's rebound speed (8u/3)f; M1 no collision if (8u/3)f ≤ 5u/6 (speed of Q ≤ speed of P); A1 0 < f ≤ 5/16 (MS p.13)
parts.er: Most correctly used the wall impact law and compared speeds, but fully correct answers were rare: equal speeds were often excluded and few said Q must rebound (f > 0) (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Given f = 1/4, find in terms of m and u the magnitude of the impulse received by Q from the wall
parts.ms: M1 I = 2m(y − (−¼y)) with mass 2m and the impact law; A1 20mu/3 (−20mu/3 → 20mu/3 condoned) (MS p.13)
parts.er: Common errors were using mass m not 2m and ignoring Q's change of direction; the magnitude must be positive (ER p.6)

parts.ask: P moves on a line with x = 2t³ − 21t² + 60t (t > 0): find the values of t when P is instantaneously at rest
parts.ms: M1 v = dx/dt, at least two powers down (dividing by t is M0); A1 v = 6t² − 42t + 60; M1 solve v = 0 for both values, t² − 7t + 10 = 0; A1 2 and 5 (MS p.7)
parts.er: Mostly correct; errors came from using calculators to solve the quadratic when dividing by 6 gives a simple equation; a few divided by t instead of differentiating (ER p.3)

parts.ask: Find the distance travelled for 1 ≤ t ≤ 3
parts.ms: M1 |x(2) − x(1)| + |x(3) − x(2)| with their stationary t inside the interval (x(1) = 41, x(2) = 52, x(3) = 45); A1 11 + 7 = 18 (MS p.7)
parts.er: Many did not split the interval at the change of direction (t = 2), so x(2) played no part; others had the right strategy but made arithmetic errors (ER pp.3–4)

parts.ask: Find the magnitude of the acceleration when t = 3
parts.ms: M1 a = dv/dt = 12t − 42; A1 6 (MS p.7)
parts.er: Many found a = −6 and did not state the magnitude; negative answers were common (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Particle Q (0.5 kg) moving with velocity (3i + j) m/s receives an impulse (2i + 5j) N s: find its speed immediately afterwards
parts.final_form: speed √170 = 13 m/s or better (13.038…), a scalar
parts.ms: M1 I = mv − mu (wrong order condoned, 5 for 0.5 condoned); A1 2i + 5j = 0.5(v − (3i + j)), v = 7i + 11j; M1 Pythagoras; A1 √170 (MS p.8)
parts.er: Almost all linked impulse to change in momentum; a few subtracted in the wrong order; several left the answer as a velocity when speed was asked (ER p.4)

parts.ask: The direction of motion of Q is turned through θ°: find θ
parts.final_form: θ = 39.1 (39 or better; 39.0938…); 321 also accepted; 0.682 rad is M1A0
parts.ms: M1 correct trig, e.g. θ = tan⁻¹(11/7) − tan⁻¹(1/3), or scalar product or cosine rule; A1 39.1 (MS p.8)
parts.er: All three scheme methods were common; errors were mostly finding the angle between the impulse and a velocity, or between a velocity and i or j (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Block (2 kg) pushed at constant speed 6 m up a line of greatest slope AB of a rough ramp (sin α = 3/7, μ = 1/3) by a force parallel to AB: use the model to find the total work done
parts.final_form: 85.8 J or 86 J (3 or 2 s.f. only)
parts.ms: M1 F_max = (1/3)(2g cos α) (= 5.90…); M1 work against friction = 6F_max (35.4 J); M1 PE gain 2g × 6 sin α (50.4 J); DM1 total = both terms, no extras; A1 85.8. Resolving along the slope but never multiplying by 6 scores the first M1 only (MS p.9)
parts.er: Most stated the friction correctly and many multiplied by the distance and found the PE gain; common errors were losing the factor 6 in one element, giving only the work against friction, or including the PE gain twice; very few confused sine and cosine (ER p.4)

parts.command: Use the work-energy principle to find
parts.ask: The block is released from rest at B: use the model and the work-energy principle to find its speed when it reaches A
parts.ms: M1 work-energy equation (KE gained = GPE lost − work against friction), all terms; A1 at most one error; A1 ½·2v² = 2g·6 sin α − 6(1/3)(2g cos α); A1 3.87 (MS p.9)
parts.er: Many correct; most common errors were sign errors from leaving weight and friction acting in the same direction, or omitting an element of the work-energy equation (ER p.4)

parts.ask: Uniform rectangle ABCD (DC = 4a, AD = 5a) folded along ST (S on AB, T on BC, SB = BT = 3a) to form lamina L: show its centre of mass is d = 71a/40 from AD
parts.final_form: printed result; final answer must be written "d = 71a/40", at least one line collecting terms
parts.ms: B1 mass ratios for a correct division with total 20a² (e.g. rectangle 20a², minus triangle 9a²/2, plus folded triangle 9a²/2); B1 distances from AD (2a, 3a, 2a, or equivalent); M1 moments about AD or a parallel axis; A1 e.g. 40a³ − (9a²/2)(3a) + (9a²/2)(2a) = 20a²d; A1* (MS p.10)
parts.er: Most efficient: square minus a triangle plus a triangle, or two rectangles plus a double-density triangle; two-stage methods often went wrong; many lost the final mark for insufficient working or for writing x̄ = 71a/40 without ever mentioning d (ER pp.4–5)

parts.ask: L has weight 4W; a particle of weight W is attached at C; L is freely suspended from S and held with AD vertical by a force F parallel to DC applied at D: find F in terms of W
parts.ms: M1 moments about S giving an equation in W and F only (moments about A is M0 unless the reaction at S is included); A1 at most one error; A1 4W(31a/40) + W(3a) = F(5a); A1 61W/50 (MS p.10)
parts.er: Many wasted time finding the vertical distance of the centre of mass from S, angles that were not needed, or the combined centre of mass; those taking moments about A rarely included the force at S (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Van (600 kg) towing a trailer (200 kg) up a road inclined at α (sin α = 1/14); non-gravitational resistances 250 N (van) and 150 N (trailer); at 16 m/s the engine works at 10 kW: find the deceleration of the van
parts.final_form: 0.419 or 0.42 m s⁻², stated as a positive deceleration
parts.ms: M1 F = 10000/16 (= 625); M1 equation of motion for the whole system, all terms; A1 at most one error; A1 F − 400 − 800g sin α = 800a; A1 0.419 (cos for sin for both vehicles is one repeated error) (MS p.11)
parts.er: Almost all used P = Fv correctly; many got a negative acceleration and did not give the deceleration as positive; other errors were missing terms, including a total mass of 600 kg (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Find the tension in the towbar at this instant
parts.ms: M1 equation of motion for van or trailer alone (mass in ma decides which); A1 at most one error; A1 T − 150 − 200g sin α = 200a or F − T − 250 − 600g sin α = 600a; A1 206 (MS p.11)
parts.er: More challenging; most formed an equation for one part but several used the wrong resistance or none; sign errors were common (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Uniform beam AB (40 N, 7 m) with A on rough horizontal ground rests on a smooth peg at C (AC = 5 m), sin θ = 3/5; normal reaction at C is P newtons: show P = 22.4
parts.final_form: printed result; the value of cos θ used must be seen
parts.ms: M1 moments about A; A1 5P = 40 × 3.5 cos θ; A1* with cos θ = 4/5 shown (MS p.12)
parts.er: Most formed a correct moments equation about A, but many simply stated the answer without the value substituted for cos θ and scored only 2 marks; a few treated the reaction at C as vertical (ER p.5)

parts.ask: Using the model, find the magnitude of the resultant force on the beam at A
parts.ms: M1 first equation (e.g. horizontal); A1 H = P sin θ (13.44); M1 second equation (e.g. vertical); A1 V + P cos θ = 40 (V = 22.08); DM1 R = √(H² + V²); A1 26. Alts: resolve parallel/perpendicular (X = 24, Y = 9.6), moments about C, B or G, or a three-force triangle with the cosine rule (MS pp.12–13)
parts.er: Many fully correct horizontal/vertical resolutions; some found only the vertical component at A; those resolving along/perpendicular to the beam or taking a second moment often used only part of the force at A; the three-force approach was concise when used (ER p.5)

parts.ask: P (m, speed 6u) and Q (5m, speed u) move in the same direction; P hits Q and P's direction is reversed; speeds afterwards x and y; coefficient e: find the complete range of e
parts.final_form: 11/25 < e ≤ 1 (A0 for an incorrect upper limit; < 1 allowed)
parts.ms: M1 CLM (6u and u opposite is a sign error); A1 6mu + 5mu = 5my − mx; M1 impact law; A1 x + y = 5eu; DM1 solve: 6x = 25eu − 11u; DM1 x > 0 gives 25e > 11; A1 cso (MS p.14)
parts.er: Many ignored that the particles start in the same direction or that P is reversed, giving wrong equations or a wrong inequality for x; several had both correct equations but could not see how to get the range of e (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Given e = 3/5, find the total kinetic energy lost in the collision
parts.final_form: 20mu²/3 (accept 6.7mu² or better); must include m and u²
parts.ms: B1 x = 2u/3, y = 7u/3; M1 KE before − KE after with correct masses and speeds; A1ft ½m·36u² + ½·5m·u² − ½m(4u²/9) − ½·5m(49u²/9); A1 20mu²/3 (MS p.14)
parts.er: Some never expressed x and y in u (method mark only); many lost the final mark by dropping m or u²; treating the particles separately (one gains KE) caused sign errors (ER p.6)

parts.ask: Q then hits a smooth fixed wall perpendicular to its motion (coefficient f) and rebounds; given there is a second collision between P and Q, find the complete range of f
parts.ms: B1ft Q's rebound speed f(7u/3); DM1 second collision if fy > x: (7/3)fu > (2/3)u; A1 2/7 < f ≤ 1 (MS p.14)
parts.er: Good understanding of the second-collision condition, most scored at least 2 of 3; both limits with correct inequalities were needed for the last mark (ER p.6)

parts.ask: P projected from A on horizontal ground with velocity (4i + 7j) m/s, landing at B: find AB
parts.final_form: 5.71 m or 5.7 m (3 or 2 s.f.; 40/7 or 56/g scores A0)
parts.ms: M1 time of flight, e.g. −7 = 7 − gt; A1 t = 14/g (1.428…); DM1 horizontal distance 4t; A1 5.71. Alt: speed √65, angle tan⁻¹(7/4), R = u² sin 2α/g (MS p.15)
parts.er: Most common error was an over-specified answer after substituting for g; some lacked a strategy for the time or confused the components (ER p.6)

parts.ask: The speed of P is less than 5 m/s for an interval of length T seconds: find T
parts.final_form: T = 0.612 or 0.61 s (30/49 or 6/g scores A0)
parts.ms: B1 vertical component 3 (speed 5 = √(4² + 3²)); M1 −3 = 3 − gT, i.e. T = 14/g − 2(4/g); A1 0.612 (MS p.15)
parts.er: Those who first found the vertical component for speed 5 usually succeeded; some found the interval but not its length, some over-specified, a significant minority used 5 m/s in a suvat equation; energy methods also worked (ER p.6)

parts.ask: When P's direction of motion is perpendicular to its initial direction it is h m above the ground: find h
parts.final_form: h = 2.23 or 2.2 (3 or 2 s.f.); cso with a negative vertical component
parts.ms: M1 scalar product of (4, 7) and (4, p) = 0; A1 p = −16/7, v = 4i − (16/7)j; DM1 (16/7)² = 7² − 2gh (or t = 65/(7g), h = 7t − ½gt²); A1 2.23 (MS p.15)
parts.er: Many found the perpendicular velocity correctly; some stated a positive vertical component without showing they knew P was moving down; a diagram would have helped (ER p.6)

parts.ask: A (2 kg) with velocity 5j m/s and B (3 kg) with velocity (3i − j) m/s collide on a smooth horizontal plane; afterwards A has velocity (3i + 2j): find the total KE before the collision
parts.ms: M1 sum of the two KE terms (modulus used correctly; 2 kg/3 kg confusion allowed for M); A1 ½·2·5² + ½·3·(3² + 1²); A1 40 (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Find, in terms of i and j, the impulse received by A
parts.final_form: I = 6i − 6j N s (in i, j form; 2(3i − 3j) accepted)
parts.ms: M1 change in momentum of A with mass 2 (either order); A1 6i − 6j, ISW (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Given the impulses on A and B are equal and opposite, find the velocity of B after the collision
parts.final_form: v_B = i + j m/s (column vector accepted)
parts.ms: M1 impulse-momentum for B with mass 3 using the negative of (b) (or CLM with plus signs); A1ft 3(v_B − (3i − j)) = −6i + 6j; A1 i + j (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Speed of P is the continuous function v = √(2t + 1) for 0 ≤ t ≤ k and v = 3t/4 for t > k (show all stages; no calculator technology): show that k = 4, explaining the method
parts.final_form: printed result k = 4 with the negative root rejected and the reason stated
parts.ms: M1 equate the two expressions at t = k (M1 only if they just verify k = 4); A1 9t² − 32t − 16 = 0; A1* t = 4 or −4/9, reject the negative since k > 0 (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Find the acceleration when t = 1.5
parts.ms: M1 differentiate √(2t + 1), power down by 1 (wrong chain rule condoned); A1 a = ½(2t + 1)^{−1/2}·2; A1 0.5 (MS p.8)

parts.ask: P passes O at t = 0: find the distance of P from O when t = 8
parts.ms: M1 integrate √(2t + 1), power up by 1, working shown; A1 (1/3)(2t + 1)^{3/2}; M1 correct use of limits 0 and 4 (C = −1/3); A1 26/3 (8.7 or better); M1 integrate 3t/4 (suvat from 3 m/s allowed); A1 (3/8)(64 − 16) = 18; A1 80/3. SC vector approach M1A1M0A0M1A0A0 (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Uniform disc C (centre X, radius R) with a disc of centre Y, radius r removed, where XY = R − r (internally tangent); the template's centre of mass is kr from X: show r = kR/(1 − k)
parts.ms: B1 area ratios πR², πr², π(R² − r²) and distances 0, R − r, kr; M1 moments about X (or a parallel axis), all terms; A1 −πr²(R − r) = (πR² − πr²)(−kr), the template on the opposite side of X; A1* via r/(R + r) = k. Using x̄ never replaced by kr scores B0M1A0A0 (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Hence find the range of possible values of k
parts.final_form: 0 < k < 1/2 (only the right-hand value needed; A0 with a wrong left-hand value)
parts.ms: M1 use 0 < kR/(1 − k) < R; A1 k < 1/2 (MS p.9)

parts.ask: P on the outer edge with PX perpendicular to XY; the template is freely suspended from P; k = 4/9: find the angle XY makes with the vertical
parts.ms: B1 r = 4R/5 (may be implied); M1 trig in a correct triangle, tan α = R/(kr) = 45/16 (finding 90° − α also earns M1); A1 70 (MS p.9)

parts.ask: The template has mass M: find the mass of the lightest particle that could be attached so the template hangs from P with XY horizontal
parts.ms: M1 moments about an axis through P: M₁gR = Mg × (distance kr), sign errors and missing g condoned; A1 M₁gR = Mg(4/9)(4R/5); A1 16M/45 (MS p.10)

parts.final_form: printed result 4mg/35, correct trig value must be seen
parts.ms: M1 F = μmg cos α (sin/cos condoned); A1* (1/7)mg(4/5) = 4mg/35 (MS p.11)

parts.command: Use the work-energy principle to find
parts.ask: Given u = √(10ag), use the work-energy principle to find AB in terms of a
parts.ms: M1 PE gain + work against friction = KE lost, all terms; A1 at most one error; A1 (4mg/35)d + mgd(3/5) = ½m(10ag); A1 7a (MS p.11)

parts.command: Use the work-energy principle to find
parts.ask: Use the work-energy principle to find, in terms of a and g, the speed of P when it returns to A
parts.ms: M1 energy equation with all terms; A1ft (4mg/35)(14a) = ½m(10ag) − ½mV², or (4mg/35)(7a) = mg(7a)(3/5) − ½mV², at most one error, ft their AB; A1ft correct; A1 √(34ag/5) (MS p.11)

parts.ask: P (m) projected at u towards Q (2m) at rest on a smooth plane; coefficient of restitution e; P's direction is reversed: find P's speed after the collision in terms of u and e
parts.ms: M1 CLM (or equal and opposite impulses); A1 mu = −mv + 2mw; M1 impact law the right way round; A1 eu = v + w; DM1 solve for v; A1 u(2e − 1)/3. v consistently in the wrong direction giving u(1 − 2e)/3 is treated as a misread (M1A0M1A0M1A1) unless corrected (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Q then hits a fixed wall perpendicular to its motion (coefficient 1/3); given there is a second collision between P and Q, find the full range of e
parts.ms: B1 Q's rebound speed x = w/3; B1 w = u(e + 1)/3; M1 their x > their v: (1/3)·u(e + 1)/3 > u(2e − 1)/3; A1 e > 1/2 (from P reversed); A1 e < 4/5 (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Uniform rod AB (mass m, length 2a) in limiting equilibrium with A on rough horizontal ground (μ = 1/3) and B against a smooth vertical wall, inclined at α to the wall: show tan α = 2/3
parts.final_form: printed result tan α = 2/3 from correct working
parts.ms: B1 F = R/3; then one resolution paired with one moments equation: B1 S = F (= mg/3) with M1A1 moments about A, S·2a cos α = mga sin α (or about G), or B1 R = mg with M1A1 moments about B; M1 solve for tan α; A1*. parts.ask: A horizontal force kmg is applied at A towards the wall, perpendicular to it; the rod remains in equilibrium in the same position: find the largest possible k
parts.ms: M1 R = mg with moments about A; A1 N = S = mg/3; DM1 resolve horizontally with friction now limiting away from the wall: kmg = R/3 + N; A1 2/3. Alternatives: moments about B or G with tan α = 2/3 (MS p.14)
