parts.ask: Golf ball hit from O on horizontal ground with velocity (2ui + uj) m/s, first landing 80 m from O: show that u = 14
parts.ms: M1 A1 horizontal 2ut = 80; M1 A1 vertical 0 = ut − ½gt² (or −u = u − gt); DM1 solve for u, e.g. u(80/2u) = ½g(80/2u)²; A1*. Swapping components is a misread (M1A0M1A0M1A1) (MS p.15)

parts.ask: Find the total time while the ball is in the air for which its speed is greater than 7√17 m/s
parts.final_form: 1.4 or 1.43 s (2 or 3 s.f.); A0 for the exact 10/7, which follows from an approximate g
parts.ms: M1 vertical component when speed is 7√17: v² = (7√17)² − 28²; A1 v = 7; DM1 suvat for the relevant time (check the logic of > versus <); A1 7 = 14 − gt, t = 0.71…; A1 total 2 × 5/7 = 1.4 or 1.43. Alts: energy gives h = 7.5 and t = 5/7, 15/7; or an equation in t directly (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: v = 3(t + 2)² i + 5t(t + 2) j for t ≥ 0 (show all stages; no calculator technology); at t = 0, r = (−30i − 45j) m: find the position vector when t = 3
parts.final_form: r = 87i + 45j m (column vector accepted; A0 for poor notation such as 87i and 45j inside a column)
parts.ms: M1 integrate, powers up by 1 in both components (M0 for suvat); A1 (t³ + 6t² + 12t)i + (5t³/3 + 5t²)j (+C); DM1 find the constant from r(0) = −30i − 45j before substituting t = 3 (or definite integration added to r(0)); A1 87i + 45j, ISW if |r| found (MS pp.7–8)

parts.ask: Find the magnitude of the acceleration when t = 3
parts.ms: M1 differentiate, powers down in both components (M0 for suvat); A1 a = (6t + 12)i + (10t + 10)j; DM1 t = 3 and Pythagoras √(30² + 40²); A1 50 (MS pp.7–8)

parts.ask: At time T, P moves in the direction of 2i + j: find T
parts.ms: M1 ratio of components: 3(T + 2)² = 10T(T + 2), an equation in T only; A1 6/7 (MS pp.7–8)

parts.ask: Particle Q (3 kg) moving at 5i m/s receives a horizontal impulse of magnitude 3√82 N s; afterwards its velocity is (xi + yj) m/s with x, y > 0, and its KE has increased by 138 J: find the velocity after the impulse
parts.final_form: v = 6i + 9j m/s (column vector accepted; ISW if speed found)
parts.ms: M1 impulse = difference in momenta, both components; A1 I = 3(xi + yj) − 3(5i); M1 Pythagoras with 3√82: 9((x − 5)² + y²) = 738; M1 change in KE equation in x and y (M0 if velocity used, two KE terms needed); A1 ½·3(x² + y² − 25) = 138; DM1 solve (x² + y² = 117 and (x − 5)² + y² = 82 give 10x = 60); A1 6i + 9j. Alt: I = 3√82(cos β, sin β) with β = 83.66… (MS pp.9–10)

parts.ask: Van (900 kg) towing a trailer (200 kg) up a road inclined at α (sin α = 1/25) by a light rigid towbar; non-gravitational resistances 400 N (van) and 240 N (trailer); engine at 15 kW: find the acceleration when the speed is 12 m/s
parts.ms: M1 equation of motion for the whole system (or two equations combined), all terms; A1 at most one error; A1 F − 640 − 1100g sin α = 1100a; M1 F = 15000/12 (= 1250); A1 0.16 or 0.163. Misusing sin α = 1/25 is an accuracy, not method, error; g = 9.81 or 10 and over-accuracy each penalised once per question (MS p.11)

parts.command: Use the work-energy principle to find
parts.ask: At 14 m/s the towbar breaks as the trailer passes A; the trailer moves up the slope to rest at B, resistance still 240 N: use the work-energy principle to find AB
parts.final_form: AB = 62 m or 61.6 m (2 or 3 s.f.)
parts.ms: M1 work-energy equation for the trailer only: KE, GPE and work done, no repeats (M0 for suvat); A1 at most one error; A1 ½·200·14² = 240d + 200g·d/25; A1 62 or 61.6 (MS p.11)

parts.final_form: printed result, extracted as "d = 17a/12"; some simplification must be seen
parts.ms: B1 mass ratio 15a² : 3a² (two triangles) : 18a²; B1 distances 3a/2 and a from AD (or a parallel axis); M1 moments about AD, all terms (vector form accepted); A1 15a²(3a/2) + 3a²·a = 18a²·d; A1* 51a/2 = 18d (MS pp.12–13)

parts.ask: The trapezium is cut as a hole from rectangle PQRS (PQ = 5a, QR = 9a), with AD parallel to and a above PS and A a from PQ; the template is freely suspended from P and hangs with PS at θ° to the downward vertical: find θ
parts.ms: B1 x̄ = 9a/2 from PQ; M1 moments about PS (or a parallel axis) for the remaining lamina, all terms; A1 at most one error; A1 27a²·ȳ = 45a²(2.5a) − 18a²(a + 17a/12); A1 ȳ = 23a/9 (2.6a or better); M1 trig for the angle with their distances (reciprocal allowed); A1 tan θ = (23a/9)/(9a/2) = 46/81, θ = 29.6 (MS pp.12–13)

parts.final_form: printed result, with "XY =" and g recovered if 9.8 used
parts.ms: M1 A1 horizontal distance u cos θ·t; M1 A1 vertical motion equation in t, u, g, θ, e.g. u sin θ·t − ½gt² = 0 (M0 if t = 2u sin θ/g or u sin θ/g is just quoted); DM1 solve for the distance; A1* XY = u cos θ·2u sin θ/g = u² sin 2θ/g (MS pp.14–15)

parts.ask: Q is projected from A at 20 m/s at 60°, passes over a vertical pole CD (5 m tall, C on the ground 12 m from A) and lands at B: find CB
parts.ms: M1 complete method using the result of (a) or first principles: 20² sin 120°/g − 12; A1 23 or 23.3 (MS pp.14–15)

parts.ask: Find the height of Q above D when Q passes over the pole
parts.ms: M1 horizontal motion for t; A1 12 = 20 cos 60°·t (t = 1.2; if t = 1.2 is found earlier it must be used here); M1 vertical motion 20 sin 60°(1.2) − ½g(1.2)² (− 5); A1 8.7 or 8.73 (MS pp.14–15)

parts.final_form: printed result k = 56/13, trig and Rc replaced, at least one line of working (no embedded value)
parts.ms: M1 moments about A, all terms, perpendicular distances (sign and sin/cos condoned); A1 at most one error; A1 5W·6a cos θ + W·12a cos θ = 9a·kW; A1* (30 + 12)(12/13) = 9k (MS pp.16–17)

parts.ask: The beam is in limiting equilibrium with coefficient of friction μ at A: find μ
parts.ms: M1 first relevant equation; A1 e.g. R + kW cos θ = 6W (R = 342W/169); M1 second relevant equation (at least one a resolution); A1 e.g. F = kW sin θ (= 280W/169); DM1 F = μR; A1 280/342 = 140/171. parts.ask: P (5m, speed 2u) and Q (2m, speed 3u) move towards each other and collide; afterwards speeds x and y, Q reversed; coefficient of restitution e: find the set of values of e for which P's direction is unchanged
parts.ms: M1 CLM; A1 10mu − 6mu = 5mx + 2my; M1 impact law the right way round; A1 y − x = 5ue; DM1 eliminate y: x = (4u − 10eu)/7; DM1 x > 0 gives an inequality in e; A1 0 ≤ e < 2/5 (MS pp.18–19)

parts.ask: In the collision Q receives an impulse of magnitude 60mu/7: show that e = 1/5
parts.ms: M1 impulse-momentum for one particle; A1 60mu/7 = 2m(3u + y) or −60mu/7 = 5m(x − 2u); DM1 solve: y = 9u/7 or x = 2u/7; M1 use CLM/impact law with x and y to form an equation in e; A1* 5ue = 9u/7 − 2u/7 (MS pp.18–19)

parts.ask: Q then hits a smooth fixed wall perpendicular to its motion (coefficient 1/3), rebounds and collides with P again: find, in terms of m and u, the magnitude of the impulse received by Q in the second collision
parts.ms: B1ft Q's rebound speed (1/3)(9u/7) = 3u/7; M1 complete method: CLM and impact law (e = 1/5) for the second collision, then impulse-momentum for one particle, e.g. I = 2m(9u/49 − (−3u/7)); A1 60mu/49 (MS pp.18–20)

parts.final_form: 290 J (2 or 3 s.f.; do not ISW)
parts.ms: M1 gain in GPE 2.6g × 20 sin α; M1 F_max = (1/5)(2.6g)(12/13); M1 work against friction = 20F_max (independent); DM1 add the two; A1 290. Omitting g is an accuracy error (MS p.7)

parts.ask: P has r = (3t + 2 − 2√(t + 1))i + (t² − 6t)j for t > 0 (show all stages; no calculator technology): find its speed when moving in the direction of i
parts.final_form: speed 2.5 m/s, a scalar (A0 for 2.5i); t = 3
parts.ms: M1 differentiate (at least 3 powers going down); A1 one component; A1 v = (3 − (t + 1)^{−1/2})i + (2t − 6)j; M1 j-component = 0 gives t = 3 (clear attempt to differentiate needed); A1 2.5 (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Find the magnitude of the acceleration when t = 0.25
parts.ms: M1 differentiate v (powers down, a constant goes to zero); A1 a = ½(t + 1)^{−3/2} i + 2j; DM1 Pythagoras at t = 0.25 (4/√125 i + 2j); A1 2.03 (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Show that P never returns to O
parts.final_form: conclusion with justification: no t > 0 makes both components of r zero
parts.ms: M1 set r = 0: j-component gives t = 6 (t = 0 excluded); A1 but the i-component at t = 6 is 20 − 2√7 ≠ 0, so P never returns (or 3t + 2 = 2√(t + 1) gives 9t² + 8t = 0 with no solution t > 0). Alternative: horizontal velocity always > 2. An argument based only on acceleration is unlikely to work (MS p.9)

parts.ask: P projected from B, 10 m vertically above A on horizontal ground, with velocity (xi + yj) m/s (x, y > 0); just before hitting the ground at C its velocity is (3i − 15j) m/s: find x and y
parts.ms: B1 x = 3; M1 suvat (or energy) equation in y, sign errors condoned; A1 15² = y² + 2g(10); A1 y = 5.4 or 5.39 (y² = 29). Horizontal/vertical confusion is not a misread. Alt: conservation of energy with all three terms (MS p.10)

parts.ask: Find the distance AC
parts.final_form: AC = 6.2 m or 6.24 m (2 or 3 s.f.)
parts.ms: M1 complete suvat for the time from B to C with their vertical speed; A1ft −15 = 5.39 − gt (t = 2.08) or equivalent; DM1 horizontal distance = their x × their t; A1 6.2 or 6.24. Over-accuracy penalised once per question (MS p.10)

parts.ask: Particle Q (2 kg) moving at 4i m/s receives a horizontal impulse I of magnitude 4√10 N s; afterwards its velocity is λ(i + j) m/s, λ > 0: find λ
parts.ms: M1 impulse-momentum with subtraction (wrong order condoned); A1 I = 2λ(i + j) − 2(4i) = (2λ − 8)i + 2λj; DM1 Pythagoras: 160 = (2λ − 8)² + (2λ)²; A1 λ² − 4λ − 12 = 0 or equivalent; A1 6. Alt: vector triangle with cosine rule. SC working with −I can score 5/5 here (MS p.11)

parts.ask: Find I in terms of i and j
parts.final_form: I = 4i + 12j (not a column vector, not in λ)
parts.ms: B1ft (2λ − 8)i + 2λj with their λ (MS p.11)

parts.ask: The angle between the impulse and Q's initial direction of motion is θ°: find θ
parts.ms: M1 trig or scalar product with their I (both components non-zero), e.g. tan θ = 12/4 (not the reciprocal); A1 72 or better from correct work (MS p.11)

parts.ask: Template = rectangle ABCD (AB = 8a, AD = ka) with isosceles triangle AED (height 6a, AE = DE) removed: show the centre of mass is d = 26a/5 from AD
parts.ms: B1 area ratios 8ka² : 3ka² : 5ka²; B1 distances 4a, 2a from AD (or parallel axis); M1 moments about AD, all terms; A1 8ka²·4a − 3ka²·2a = 5ka²·d; A1* (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Two identical rectangles (8a by ½ka), each with three times the template's mass per unit area, are attached along AB and DC to form model PQRSDEA, freely suspended from P, hanging with PS at θ to the downward vertical: find tan θ exactly in terms of k
parts.ms: M1 moments about PS (or parallel axis) using the factor 3 with the areas (5ka², 15ka², 15ka² is M0; one slip allowed); A1 at most one slip; A1 5k·(26a/5) + 2·3·4k·4a = (5k + 24k)x̄; A1 x̄ = 122a/29; B1 ȳ = ka from PQ; A1ft tan θ = x̄/ȳ = 122/(29k) (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Uniform rod AB (8a, weight 12W) freely hinged at A to a vertical wall, particle W at B; string of length 5a from C on the rod (AC = 5a) to D on the wall above A (AD = 8a), angle DAC = angle ADC = θ: show the tension is T = 7W
parts.final_form: printed result T = 7W; the working must show where the lengths come from and each term needs a trig ratio
parts.ms: M1 moments about A (or another complete method), all terms, sign and sin/cos condoned; A1 at most one error; A1 12W·4a sin θ + W·8a sin θ = 5a·T sin 2θ (or = 3aT cos θ + 4aT sin θ), with sin θ = 3/5, cos θ = 4/5; A1* 56W = 8T. No trig in the moments equation is M0 (given answer, no benefit of doubt) (MS p.13)

parts.ask: The force on the rod at the hinge A acts at α° above the rod (0 < α < 90): find α
parts.final_form: α = 7.3 (7.29205… or better); 0.127 rad treated as a misread
parts.ms: M1 first equation (e.g. resolve horizontally); A1 H = T sin θ = 21W/5; M1 second equation (e.g. vertically); A1 V + T cos θ = 13W (V = 37W/5); DM1 complete method, e.g. α = tan⁻¹(V/H) − tan⁻¹(4/3); A1 7.3. Alternatives: resolve parallel/perpendicular to the rod, moments about C or B (MS p.13)

parts.ask: P (mass m, speed 6u) and Q (mass km, speed u) move towards each other and collide; afterwards P has speed 2v (same direction) and Q speed 3v (reversed); e = 1/3: find v in terms of u
parts.ms: M1 impact law the right way round; A1 (3v − 2v)/(6u + u) = 1/3; A1 7u/3. v/(5u) = 1/3 is treated as a sign slip, M1A0A0 (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Find k
parts.ms: M1 CLM (or equal and opposite impulses), one slip in pairing allowed, consistent omission of m condoned; A1 6mu − kmu = 3kmv + 2mv; A1 1/6 (MS p.14)

parts.ask: Q then hits a smooth fixed wall perpendicular to its motion (coefficient f) and rebounds; the first P–Q collision is a distance d from the wall and the second is d/7 from the wall: find f
parts.ms: B1ft Q's rebound speed 3vf (= 7uf); B1ft P's time between collisions (6d/7)/(2v); M1 Q's time d/(3v) + (d/7)/(3fv); DM1 equate times and solve; A1 1/2. Alternatives: time from wall impact to second collision, or distances travelled (MS pp.14–16)

parts.ask: P starts from rest at O; acceleration k(3 − t²) m/s² (k > 0); speed 13.5 m/s when t = 1.5 (no calculator technology, show all stages): show k = 4
parts.final_form: printed result k = 4; substitution of 1.5 and 13.5 must be seen; t = 0, v = 0 must be referred to
parts.ms: M1 integrate a with both powers up by 1; A1 v = k(3t − t³/3) (+C); A1* C = 0 from t = 0, v = 0 and k(3 × 1.5 − 1.5³/3) = 13.5 gives k = 4 (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Show that the displacement is s = (1/3)t²(18 − t²)
parts.final_form: printed result, including "s ="; any equivalent factorised form
parts.ms: M1 integrate their v (from integrating a), both powers up by 1, k need not be substituted; A1* s = 4(3t²/2 − t⁴/12) = (1/3)t²(18 − t²), with reference to s = 0 at t = 0 (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Find the total distance P moves before it returns to O
parts.ms: M1 v = 0 to find t; A1 t = 3; M1 s at their non-zero t (from v = 0) gives 27; A1 54 (out 27 m and back). t = 3 may come from a correct sketch of v (MS pp.7–8)

parts.ms: M1 differentiate r (both powers down by 1, must be a vector); A1 v = 2t^{−1/2} i − 3j; M1 t = 4 gives i − 3j; M1 impulse-momentum (M0 if g included, mass 3 missing, or r at t = 4 used); A1 6i − 3j = 3(v − (i − 3j)) gives v = 3i − 4j; M1 Pythagoras; A1 5 (MS p.9)

parts.ask: Uniform wire framework: semicircular arcs AB (radius 2a) and CD (radius a), both centre O, joined by straight wires AC and DB (each a), ACDB a straight line (arc centre-of-mass formula 2r/π given): show the centre of mass is 6a/(3π + 2) from AB
parts.final_form: printed result 6a/(3π + 2) (any equivalent form with whole numbers); AC and DB must appear
parts.ms: B1 length ratios 2πa : πa : 2a : (3π + 2)a; B1 distances from AB 4a/π, 2a/π, 0; M1 moments about AB (or parallel axis), all terms; A1 2πa(4a/π) − πa(2a/π) = (3πa + 2a)d (arc CD on the opposite side); A1* given answer. Treating it as a lamina scores at most B0B0M1A0A0 (MS pp.10–11)

parts.ask: E is on arc AB with angle AOE = 90°; the framework is freely suspended from A and hangs with AE at θ to the downward vertical: find the exact value of tan θ, simplified
parts.final_form: tan θ = (3π − 1)/(3π + 5), exact and simplified (π and integers)
parts.ms: B1 tan OAG = [6a/(3π + 2)]/2a = 3/(3π + 2) (B0 if OAG called θ); M1 tan θ = tan(45° − β) or equivalent (arctan 1 allowed); DM1 correct compound-angle formula; DM1 substitute tan β; A1 (3π − 1)/(3π + 5). Alt: drop a perpendicular from G to AE (MS pp.10–11)

parts.ask: Car of mass 750 kg up a line of greatest slope (sin α = 1/7), non-gravitational resistance 200 N, engine at 20 kW: find the constant speed at which it could move up the slope
parts.ms: M1 P = Fv (wrong number of zeros condoned); M1 equation of motion with zero acceleration, sign and sin/cos condoned; A1 20000/V − 750g sin α − 200 = 0; A1 16 (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Find the acceleration at the instant the car moves up the slope at 10 m/s
parts.ms: M1 equation of motion with correct terms; A1 at most one error; A1 2000 − 750g sin α − 200 = 750a; A1 1 (MS p.12)

parts.command: Use the work-energy principle to find
parts.ask: At that instant (point A) the engine is switched off; resistance still 200 N: using the work-energy principle, find how far up the slope from A the car travels before coming to rest
parts.ms: M1 work-energy equation, dimensionally correct, sign errors condoned, h and d allowed (M0 for ½·750·10² − 750gh = 200h); A1 at most one error; A1 ½·750·10² − 750g·d sin α = 200d; A1 30. Using 16 instead of 10 is an accuracy error (MS p.12)

parts.ask: P (2m) moving at u hits Q (m) at rest on a smooth plane; coefficient of restitution e > 0: show the speed of Q after the collision is 2(1 + e)u/3
parts.final_form: printed result 2(1 + e)u/3 (any fully factorised equivalent), at least one line of intermediate working
parts.ms: M1 CLM (mark first); A1 2mu = 2m·v_P + m·v_Q; M1 impact law with e on the correct side; A1 eu = v_Q − v_P; A1* (MS pp.13–14)

parts.ask: The total loss of KE is k(1 − e²)mu²: find k
parts.final_form: k = 1/3 (accept 0.33 or better, from correct working)
parts.ms: B1 v_P = (2 − e)u/3; M1 KE after = ½(2m)v_P² + ½m·v_Q² (must add); A1 correct unsimplified; DM1 ½(2m)u² − KE after (final − initial condoned); A1 1/3 (MS pp.13–14)

parts.ask: The magnitude of the impulse of Q on P is 8mu/9: find e
parts.ms: M1 correct impulse-momentum equation for Q or P (sign errors not condoned), e.g. 8mu/9 = m·2(1 + e)u/3; A1 1/3 (MS pp.13–14)

parts.ask: Q then hits a fixed wall at right angles to its motion (coefficient of restitution f); afterwards Q has the same speed as P: find f
parts.ms: B1 Q's rebound speed 2(1 + e)uf/3; M1 equate to P's speed (2 − e)u/3 with their e (0 < e ≤ 1) to get an equation in f only; A1 5/8 (MS pp.13–14)

parts.ask: Uniform rod AB (mass m, length 2a) with A on rough horizontal floor rests against a smooth horizontal rail at C (AC = 1.5a), at θ to the floor: show the normal reaction at C is S = 2mg cos θ/3
parts.ms: M1 moments about A, dimensionally correct (M0 if a's missing), sin/cos and sign condoned; A1 S·1.5a = mga cos θ; A1* (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: Show that the vertical component of the force at A is V = (mg/3)(3 − 2cos²θ)
parts.ms: M1 resolve vertically; A1 V = mg − S cos θ; A1* from fully correct working. If S never seen, max M1A1A0 (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: The rod is in limiting equilibrium with coefficient of friction 4/7: show that p tan²θ + q tan θ + r = 0 and find the integers p, q, r
parts.final_form: 6 tan²θ − 7 tan θ + 2 = 0 (or an integer multiple)
parts.ms: B1 F = (4/7)V seen or implied; M1 another equation (resolving or moments), e.g. horizontal F = S sin θ; A1 correct; DM1 substitute for V and S with F = μV to get an equation in θ only; DM1 divide by cos²θ and use sec²θ = 1 + tan²θ; A1 6 tan²θ − 7 tan θ + 2 = 0. Alternatives: resolve parallel/perpendicular to the rod, moments about B, C or G (MS pp.15–16)

parts.ask: Stone projected from O at 20 m/s at α to the ground; when 11 m above the ground its vertical and horizontal velocity components have magnitudes V and 2V; model g = 10 m/s²: using conservation of mechanical energy, show V = 6
parts.final_form: printed result V = 6, obtained with g = 10
parts.ms: M1 energy equation, correct terms (M0 if energy not used; if V used directly, both components needed); A1 ½m·20² − ½mv² = mg × 11 (v² = 180); A1 ½m·20² − ½m(V² + (2V)²) = mg × 11; A1* V = 6 (MS pp.17–18)

parts.ask: The stone hits a plane inclined at 60° to the ground at A, moving perpendicular to the plane at that instant: using the model, find the height of A above the ground to 2 s.f.
parts.ms: M1 perpendicularity at A gives the speed S (sin/cos condoned); A1 S = 12/cos 30° = 8√3; M1 energy from O to A (or from the 11 m level); A1 ½m·20² − ½mS² = mgH; DM1 solve; A1 10. Alt: vertical component W = 12 tan 30° = 4√3 with suvat, W² = 16² − 2gH (or 6² − 2gs, s = −0.6) (MS pp.17–18)

parts.ask: Particle on the x-axis with x = 2t⁴ − 14t³ + (45/2)t² + 14t for 0 ≤ t ≤ 3 (solutions relying entirely on calculator technology not acceptable): verify P is instantaneously at rest when t = 2
parts.final_form: printed result: v = 0 at t = 2, from v = 8t³ − 42t² + 45t + 14
parts.ms: M1 differentiate, at least two powers of t going down by 1; A1 v = 8t³ − 42t² + 45t + 14; A1* substitute t = 2 to get v = 0, or solve v = 0 giving t = −1/4, 2, 3.5 (A0 if any wrong root appears); stating "t = 2, v = 0" with no working is A0 (MS pp.7, 7 notes)

parts.ask: Given t = 2 is the only time in 0 ≤ t ≤ 3 when P is at rest, find the total distance travelled for 0 ≤ t ≤ 3
parts.ms: M1 complete method |x(2) − x(0)| + |x(3) − x(2)| (x0 = 0, x2 = 38, x3 = 28.5), sign errors not condoned; A1 95/2 (MS p.7). The scheme's answer is printed as a stacked fraction; 95/2 is read from the printed x-values.

parts.ask: Find the magnitude of the acceleration of P when t = 1.5
parts.ms: M1 differentiate v: a = 24t² − 84t + 45; M1 substitute t = 1.5; A1 27 (MS p.7)

parts.ask: Uniform square lamina ABCD of side 2a; the semicircle on diameter AB is removed and attached to BC to form lamina L (sector formula may be used): show the centre of mass of L is x̄ = (a/24)(28 + 3π) from AD
parts.final_form: printed result x̄ = (a/24)(28 + 3π), factorised with (28 + 3π); at least one stage of simplification seen
parts.ms: B1 mass ratios 4a² : πa²/2 : πa²/2 : 4a²; B1 distances from AD a, a, 2a + 4a/3π (or from a parallel axis); M1 moments about AD or a parallel axis, all terms, dimensionally correct; A1 4a²·a − (πa²/2)·a + (πa²/2)(2a + 4a/3π) = 4a²·x̄; A1* given answer. Vector form acceptable (MS pp.8–9)

parts.ask: L has weight W; a particle of weight kW is attached at D; the loaded lamina hangs from two vertical strings at A (tension 4T) and B (tension T) with DC horizontal: find the exact value of k
parts.final_form: k = (92 + 15π)/48, exact (equivalent p + qπ forms accepted)
parts.ms: M1 moments about AD (or a parallel axis), all terms; A1 T·2a = W·(a/24)(28 + 3π), decimal x̄ accepted; M1 second relevant equation (moments or vertical equilibrium); A1 e.g. 5T = W + kW; A1 cao exact. Moments about B, the midpoint of AB or G are alternatives (MS pp.8–9)

parts.ask: Ball projected from A on horizontal ground with velocity (8i + 14j) m/s, moving freely under gravity: find the maximum height above the ground
parts.ms: M1 complete method, e.g. 0 = 14² − 2gh, sign errors condoned; A1 10 (MS pp.10–11)

parts.ask: Find the speed of the ball 2.4 s after leaving A
parts.ms: M1 vertical component 14 − 2.4g; M1 Pythagoras with both components √(8² + (14 − 2.4g)²); A1 12.4 or 12 (MS pp.10–11)

parts.ask: C is 3 m vertically above B on the ground; the ball passes through C after reaching its maximum height: find the distance AB
parts.ms: M1 vertical equation, e.g. 3 = 14t − ½gt² (sign errors condoned); A1 correct (t = 2.62…, need not be seen); M1 horizontal distance 8t; A1 uses the larger root t = 2.6…; A1 21 or 21.0. Alternatives: trajectory equation in x and y, or energy for the vertical speed (√(686/5) = 11.71…) then suvat (MS pp.10–11)

parts.ask: Cyclist and cycle (70 kg) on a level road with constant acceleration 0.4 m/s², resistance 30 N: find the rate of working when the speed is 5 m/s
parts.ms: M1 equation of motion, all terms, no extras; A1 D − 30 = 70(0.4); M1 P = D × 5; A1 290 (MS p.12)

parts.command: Use the work-energy principle to find
parts.ask: Freewheeling down a hill from A to B (AB = 250 m), speed 5 m/s at A and 8 m/s at B, resistance 30 N: use the model with the work-energy principle to find the change in vertical height
parts.ms: M1 at least one correct KE term; B1 work against resistance 250 × 30; M1 work-energy equation, all terms, no double counting, mass 70 used (sign errors condoned); A1 70gH = ½·70·8² − ½·70·5² + 250·30; A1 13 or 12.9 (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Up a hill from C to D (200 m) at constant speed 8 m/s, at 5° to the horizontal, resistance 30 N: find the total work done by the cyclist
parts.ms: M1 total work = gain in PE + work against resistance, no extras or double counting; A1 70g(200 sin 5°) + 30 × 200; A1 18000. Accuracy is penalised only once in the whole question (MS p.12)

parts.ask: Particle of mass 0.5 kg moving with velocity 6i m/s receives impulse (ai + bj) N s of magnitude 3√2/2 N s, and its direction of motion is deflected through 45°: find the two possible impulses in terms of i and j
parts.ms: M1 A1 velocity after in component form, v cos45° i ± v sin45° j (or λi ± λj); M1 A1 change in momentum in vector form 0.5v − 0.5(6i); M1 A1 magnitude of impulse gives an equation in one unknown, e.g. (3√2/2)² = (0.5v cos45° − 3)² + (0.5v sin45°)², v = 3√2 (or λ = 3); A1 one impulse in pi + qj form; A1 both. Using only one sign throughout and finding one impulse caps at M1A0M1A1M1A1A1A0 (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Uniform rod AB (mass m, length 2d) horizontal with A against a rough vertical wall, held by a light string from B to C on the wall, AC = 0.8d above A; a particle of mass km at B: show the tension is T = (mg√29/4)(2k + 1)
parts.final_form: printed result T = (mg√29/4)(2k + 1); at least one line between the equation and the answer
parts.ms: M1 complete method for an equation in T, m, g, k and the string angle, e.g. moments about A (sign and sin/cos condoned, missing g is one accuracy error); A1 at most one error; A1 T cos α·2d = mg·d + kmg·2d; A1* given answer using cos α = 2/√29, sin α = 5/√29 (α at C) (MS pp.14–15)

parts.ask: The resultant force on the rod at A makes angle θ with the horizontal, tan θ = 1/8: find the exact value of k
parts.ms: M1 resolve vertically; A1 Y + T cos α = mg + kmg; M1 resolve horizontally; A1 X = T sin α; M1 tan θ = Y/X used to give an equation in k only (±1/8 or ±8 must be used); A1 11/10 (MS pp.14–15)

parts.ask: P (2m), Q (3m), R (5m) at rest in a line on a smooth surface, Q between; coefficient of restitution e between each pair; P projected at 2u towards Q: show Q's speed after the collision is (4u/5)(e + 1)
parts.ms: M1 CLM with correct mass-speed pairings; A1 2m(2u) = 2m(−v) + 3m(w); M1 impact law the right way round; A1 e(2u) = w + v, consistent with CLM; A1* given answer (MS pp.16–17)

parts.ask: P's direction of motion is reversed in the collision: find the full range of possible values of e
parts.ms: M1 expression for P's velocity in u and e; A1 v = (2u/5)(3e − 2) (for P reversed); A1 v > 0 gives 2/3 < e ≤ 1 (MS pp.16–17)

parts.ask: The magnitude of the impulse exerted on Q by P is 108mu/25: show e = 4/5
parts.final_form: printed result e = 4/5, at least one line of working
parts.ms: M1 impulse-momentum for Q; A1 108mu/25 = 3m·(4u/5)(e + 1); A1* (MS pp.16–17)

parts.ask: Determine, with clear reasoning, whether there will be a second collision between P and Q
parts.final_form: conclusion with reason: Q rebounds from R at 0.18u, faster than P's 0.16u in the same direction, so P and Q collide again
parts.ms: B1 P's speed after the first collision 0.16u (4u/25, ± allowed); M1 CLM for Q (1.44u) hitting R using (a), e need not be substituted; M1 impact law for Q and R the right way round; A1 Q's velocity after hitting R: x = 0.18u back towards P (e replaced); dM1 compare speeds of P (0.16u) and Q (0.18u), dependent on both M marks and velocities in u; A1 cso since 0.18u > 0.16u there will be another collision between P and Q. Merely listing the two speeds then concluding is M0A0 (MS pp.16–18)

parts.ask: Car (500 kg) towing a trailer (150 kg) on a level road by a light towbar; resistances 350 N and 200 N; engine works at 10.5 kW: find the acceleration a when the speed is 14 m/s
parts.ms: M1 equation of motion for the whole system (or both parts with T eliminated), all terms, M0 if power used as a force; A1 F − 350 − 200 = 650a; M1 F = 10500/14 (= 750), independent, M0 for just 14F = 10500 with nothing further; A1 4/13 (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Find the tension T in the towbar at that instant
parts.ms: M1 equation of motion for car or trailer alone giving an equation in T and a only (M0 if power used as a force); A1ft T − 200 = 150a or 750 − 350 − T = 500a, follow their a; A1 3200/13 (MS p.8)

parts.ask: Particle of mass 2 kg moving with velocity 4i m/s receives a horizontal impulse of magnitude √29 N s, after which its velocity is (3i + λj) m/s with λ > 0: find λ
parts.ms: M1 impulse-momentum equation, must subtract (wrong order condoned); A1 I = 2(3i + λj) − 2(4i) = 2(−i + λj); M1 magnitude of their impulse equated to √29, e.g. 29 = 4(1 + λ²); A1 λ = 2.5, positive only (MS p.9). The radical in √29 is missing from the QP text layer; confirmed on a page render (work/wme02p2/img/v2.png) and by the scheme equation 29 = 4(1 + λ²).

parts.ask: Find the angle between the direction of motion of P before the impulse and the direction of the impulse
parts.ms: M1 trig or scalar product for a relevant angle between 4i and their I (M0 if 3i + λj used, M0 for tan⁻¹ differences such as tan⁻¹(2/5) − tan⁻¹ 4); A1ft correct ratio, e.g. tan θ = 5/2 for the acute angle; A1 111.801…° (MS p.9)

parts.ask: v = (2t + 3)i + (t² − 5t − 15)j for t ≥ 0 (no calculator technology allowed, show all stages): find the acceleration when t = 4
parts.final_form: vector: 2i + 3j m s⁻² (ISW if the magnitude is also found)
parts.ms: M1 a = dv/dt, at least two powers of t going down by 1; A1 2i + 3j (MS p.10)

parts.ask: Given r = 6i − 2j when t = 1, find an exact expression for r in terms of t
parts.final_form: r = (t² + 3t + 2)i + (t³/3 − 5t²/2 − 15t + 91/6)j, exact; column vector not accepted for this answer
parts.ms: M1 r = ∫v dt, at least two powers going up by 1; A1 correct with or without constants; M1 use t = 1, r = 6i − 2j to find both constants; A1 cao exact (MS p.10)

parts.ask: At t = T, Q moves in the direction of 5i − 3j: find the exact speed of Q at that time
parts.final_form: exact speed: √306 = 3√34 m/s (decimal after the exact value is ISW); T = 6 only
parts.ms: M1 form an equation in T from velocity parallel to 5i − 3j (5 and −3 on the wrong sides condoned); A1 −3(2T + 3) = 5(T² − 5T − 15); DM1 simplify and solve 5T² − 19T − 66 = 0, (5T + 11)(T − 6) = 0, T = 6; M1 Pythagoras with their T (not available if more than one positive T is kept); A1 √306 or 3√34, must be exact (MS p.10)

parts.ask: Template = rectangle ABDE (2a × 8a) joined along BD to semicircle BCD (diameter 8a), with semicircle PQR (diameter PR = 4a on BD) removed; given the semicircle centre-of-mass formula 4r/3π: show the distance of the centre of mass from BD is d = 32a/(3(8 + 3π))
parts.final_form: printed result d = 32a/(3(8 + 3π)); must be stated as "d =" (not x̄)
parts.ms: B1 mass ratios 16 : 8π : 2π : 6π + 16; B1 distances from BD (or a parallel axis) −a, 16a/3π, 8a/3π (sign error condoned); M1 moments about BD with all terms, dimensionally consistent, correct pairings; A1 correct unsimplified equation, e.g. −16a + 8π(16a/3π) − 2π(8a/3π) = (6π + 16)d; A1* given answer from full correct working (MS p.11)

parts.ask: Template freely suspended from B hangs in equilibrium with BD at φ° to the downward vertical: find φ
parts.ms: B1 vertical distance of the centre of mass from B along BD is 4a (seen or implied); M1 trig for a relevant angle using d and 4a (M0 if 4a not used), tan φ = [32a/(3(8 + 3π))]/4a; A1 8.7 (MS p.11)

parts.ask: Template weight 15W with a particle of weight kW at E; pivoted at B and held with BD vertical by a horizontal force W at E acting towards D: find k
parts.final_form: k = (48 − 12π)/(8 + 3π) or 0.59 or better (0.59116…), or an equivalent single fraction
parts.ms: M1 moments about B (or another complete method) giving an equation in k, W and a only, all terms, dimensionally consistent, sign errors condoned; A1 at most one error; A1 correct, e.g. 15W·d − 2a·kW = 8a·W with d = 32a/(3(8 + 3π)); A1 (48 − 12π)/(8 + 3π) (MS pp.11–12)

parts.ask: Uniform rod AB (length 30a, weight W) rests in limiting equilibrium on a fixed smooth hemisphere (centre O, radius 7a) with A on rough ground, touching at C; AO = 25a: show AC = 24a
parts.ms: B1* Pythagoras √((25a)² − (7a)²) = 24a; quoting the Pythagorean triple is allowed; B0 if errors in working (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Show that the normal reaction at C has magnitude 3W/5
parts.ms: M1 moments about A (or equivalent complete method), dimensionally consistent, sin/cos confusion condoned, M0 if 25a used instead of 24a, M1A0A0 if a never appears; A1 W·15a cos θ = 24a·N; A1* N = (15/25)W = 3W/5, must see cos θ = 24/25 used (MS p.13)

parts.ask: Coefficient of friction at A is μ (limiting equilibrium): find μ
parts.ms: M1 first resolution (e.g. vertical), sign and sin/cos condoned; A1 R + N cos θ = W, R = 53W/125; M1 second resolution (horizontal); A1 F = N sin θ = 21W/125; DM1 F = μR to get an equation in μ only, using only equations that earned marks; A1 21/53. Alternatives: resolving parallel/perpendicular to the rod or moments about C, B or G (MS pp.13–14)

parts.ask: P (mass 9m) moving at 4u hits Q (mass 3m) at rest on a smooth surface; coefficient of restitution e: show Q's speed after the collision is 3u(1 + e)
parts.final_form: printed result v_Q = 3u(1 + e), with at least one line of intermediate working
parts.ms: M1 CLM, all terms, correct masses; A1 9m·4u = 9m·v_P + 3m·v_Q; M1 impact law used the right way round; A1 v_Q − v_P = 4ue; A1* given answer (MS p.15)

parts.ask: Total kinetic energy lost in the collision is kmu²; given e = 2/3, find k
parts.ms: B1 v_P = u(3 − e) = 7u/3 (or its negative), seen or implied; M1 KE lost = ½·9m(4u)² − ½·9m·v_P² − ½·3m·v_Q², all terms (all signs reversed condoned); A1ft correct expression in m and u, follow their v_P (= 18mu²(1 − e²)); A1 10 (MS p.15). e = 2/3 is read from v_P = 7u/3 in the scheme; the fraction is lost from the QP text layer.

parts.ask: Q then hits a fixed vertical wall perpendicular to its motion and receives an impulse of magnitude 21mu: find the coefficient of restitution between Q and the wall
parts.ms: B1 rebound speed w = 5uf (or −5uf), sign error condoned; M1 impulse-momentum for Q with mass 3m, e.g. 21mu = 3m·5u − 3m·w (giving w = −2u), sign error condoned; A1cso 2/5 (MS p.16)

parts.ask: Rough ramp at α to the ground (tan α = 5/12), AB = 5 m along a line of greatest slope; particle of mass 0.5 kg; coefficient of friction 1/3: find the work done against friction from A to B
parts.ms: M1 F = μR with R = 0.5g cos α, i.e. F = (1/3)(0.5g)(12/13), sin/cos confusion condoned; DM1 work done = F × 5; A1 7.5 or 7.54; 10g/13 is not accepted (MS p.17)

parts.command: Use the work-energy principle to find
parts.ask: Particle projected up the ramp from A with speed U; speed 26 m/s at B: use the work-energy principle to find U
parts.ms: M1 work-energy equation with all terms (sign errors and sin/cos condoned); A1ft at most one error; A1ft correct: ½(0.5)U² = ½(0.5)(26²) + 0.5g·5 sin α + their WD; A1 27 or 27.3 (MS p.17)

parts.ask: After leaving the ramp at B the particle moves freely; it is above the level of B for T seconds: find T
parts.ms: M1 complete suvat method; A1 correct equation, e.g. −26 sin α = 26 sin α − gT (20 = gT) or 0 = 26 sin α·T − ½gT²; A1 2.0 or 2.04 (MS p.17)

parts.ask: The particle first hits the ground at C: find the distance AC
parts.final_form: AC = 58 m or 57.8 m (2 or 3 s.f.)
parts.ms: M1 complete suvat method for the time to reach the ground (B is 5 sin α above the ground); A1 at most one error; A1 correct, e.g. −5 sin α = 26 sin α·t − ½gt² (t = 2.2177…), or time up + time down; DM1 horizontal distance 26 cos α·t (≈ 53.22); M1 add the ramp's horizontal length 5 cos α; A1 58 or 57.8 (MS pp.17–18)
